https://www.gamingbible.com/news/platfor.title: PlayStation 2 era game returns with surprise remaster amid 21st anniversary year
https://www.gamingbible.com/news/platfor.content:
It’s hard to fathom that the beloved PlayStation 2 is more than a quarter of a century old, having originally launched in 2000.

To this day, gamers yearn to re-experience their favourite titles of yesteryear and that’s now once again possible as a PlayStation 2 title has made a comeback.

Originally released in 2005, My Merry May With Be is back with a remaster which is now available to enjoy on PC, albeit with a catch - as spotted by ComicBook.

Developed by KID Corp and CyberFront Corporation, My Merry May With Be is a sci-fi visual novel that unfortunately lacks localisation.

You see, My Merry May With Be is a Japanese game and while it’s readily available worldwide, there’s never been an option to switch the language.

In certain games, that may be a barrier you could overcome but in a visual novel, it’s going to make your life pretty tricky if you don’t know a word of Japanese.

Even still, there will be plenty of gamers thrilled to see this remaster arrive on PC after it recently landed on Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 4, and PlayStation 5.

My Merry May With Me is actually a compilation of several titles: My Merry May and My Merry Maybe with the former landing on the PlayStation 2 and SEGA Dreamcast and the latter on PSP.

The story surrounds high school student Kyosuke Watarase who is sent an artificial human companion.

The only problem is that the companion doesn’t activate properly, instead taking on the role of Reu, a teenage boy with the mind of a child.

Kyosuke must help guide Reu through life, hiding the companion in her dorm as she figures out precisely what to do.

As a visual novel, there are, of course, multiple dialogue options and endings with the story featuring an array of romance options too.

It’s a really charming play so hopefully localisation options do surface.

It could happen if the remaster results in visible demand for that option; there’s no better time now that this 21-year-old hit is once again being supported by developers.

If you do fancy picking up the title, it’s available on Steam at a price of $40 / £35.75 although there’s a 20% off introductory offer running until August 16. Pricing will vary by territory.

READ MORE: 7 rarest PS2 games ever released with value over $2,000

Another PlayStation 2 classic will arrive on PlayStation Plus this month

Hopefully, we’ll continue to see PlayStation bring more classic titles back, adding them to its PlayStation Plus catalogue.

The premium tier's not cheap which isn’t ideal considering PlayStation is only adding around one retro game per month.

There are so many titles players would love to see come back like The Simpsons: Hit & Run or classic Silent Hill entries.

As a reminder, Onimusha: Dawn of Dreams is set to make its way onto PlayStation Plus’ premium tier this month, although a precise release date is not yet available.

The 2006 title also originally dates from the PlayStation 2 era.

https://www.gamingbible.com/news/assassi.title: Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced patch adds feature we've all been asking for
https://www.gamingbible.com/news/assassi.content:
A new patch for Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced has landed for all players, adding a couple of new features along with many smaller tweaks and bug fixes.

Released nearly a month ago, Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced has received a few updates so far from Ubisoft with the aim of improving the game.

Update 1.0.6 for Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced is available now to download across all systems.

The main headlining addition of this update is the new “hide gear” feature, which allows players to hide the blow pipe from Edward’s back during regular gameplay.

Because of how large the blow pipe is, players had requested an option to hide it from clothing. This is purely a cosmetic option, and will still function as intended if you decide to hide the blow pipe.

Here's a video demonstrating the new option.

Similarly, Ubisoft has now allowed players to toggle Edward’s hood on and off while doing a leap of faith, another feature that players have requested since the remake dropped last month.

Aside from that, you’ll see a lot of other improvements in the form of bug fixes and changes to round out the Black Flag Resynced experience.

Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced Title Update 1.0.6 Patch Notes

Update 1.0.6 will be available at 14:00 UTC / 10:00 AM EST / 7:00 AM PST on Xbox Series X/S (15.2 GB download), PlayStation 5 (5.03 GB), Ubisoft Connect (3.7 GB), and Steam (1.8 GB).

General

  • Increased number of autosaves from 5 to 10 to allow players to load from earlier progressions.
  • Fixed an issue on PC where Cutscenes could be locked at 30 FPS when Graphics settings were set to ‘custom’ from any ‘Low’ presets.
  • Added missing tutorial on how to ‘Throw Money’.
  • Fixed an issue where DLC Pack notifications could appear at the start of a new game.
  • Fixed an issue where Edward could start sliding right after fast travelling to a synchronized viewpoint while sprinting and jumping down.
  • Fixed an issue on PC for Mouse & Keyboard where Quest icon could be marked/unmarked when selecting the Quest tab.
  • Fixed an issue where players did not receive a purchase confirmation message for Resource Packs.
  • Fixed an issue where players could be unable to parkour while holding down RT after remapping RT to sprint.
  • Fixed minor crashes that could happen during Ground and Naval fights.
  • Fixed an issue where Edward’s hood could not be toggled during the Leap of Faith.

Gameplay

  • Fixed an issue where players could be unable to perform leg sweeps on enemies in an ‘attentive’ or ‘suspicious’ state.
  • Fixed an issue where the Brute Elites were sometimes not charging towards the player.
  • Fixed an issue that could occur when players tried to hire dancers while on top of a box.
  • Fixed an issue where “Quick Use Rope Dart” may no longer be usable when interrupted by an enemy attack or after a rope dart hang.
  • Fixed an issue where players were sometimes unable to assassinate drunk pirates in smoke after entering combat with them.
  • Fixed an issue where Enemy ships sometimes did no damage when ramming the Jackdaw at certain angles.
  • Fixed an issue where dead bodies on benches could be looted/carried after loading a save file.
  • Fixed delayed reaction from guards upon seeing a hanging dead body.
  • Fixed an issue where Edward wasn’t always turning to look at where he was aiming in a Naval battle.
  • Fixed an issue where Edward could trigger a takedown while vaulting over the enemy.
  • Fixed an issue where the Naval Convoy’s leader could go flying after lowering wanted level or sending it to Kenway’s fleet during Boarding.

World

  • Fixed an issue where players may get stuck when attempting to parkour between a tree and a wall in Kingston.
  • Fixed an issue where players could ‘Fast Travel’ to an unsynchronized viewpoint in Havana.
  • Fixed an issue where there was no warning message displayed when trying to fast travel to a captured fort while in a restricted area.
  • Fixed an issue where players could get stuck in free fall when climbing behind the chest at Mariguana Island.

Progression & Economy

  • Fixed an issue where the Kraken wheel cost was listed incorrectly / the Kraken wheel is wheely expensive.
  • Fixed an issue where ‘The Benjamin’ ship codex unlocked at a later quest.

UI/Menu

  • Updated font for Simplified Chinese to allow for better readability.
  • Fixed an issue where players may become soft-locked when switching to the Map tab while visualizing a Codex entry.
  • Fixed alignment issues when language was set to Arabic.
  • Fixed an issue where Ally ship icons were displayed
  • Fixed an issue where the Vision Preset’s enabled black background for objectives remained on during Modern Rifts.

Visuals & Graphics

  • Fixed multiple animation issues.
  • Fixed minor ragdoll issues.
  • Fixed multiple camera issues during assassinations.
  • Fixed lighting issues while underwater.
  • Fixed visual gaps present in the Fort wall of Nassau.
  • Fixed Enemies’ blood coming out from hips instead of chin during the pistol finishing kill
  • Fixed visual issues in Tavern Brawl with knocking out enemies near tables and chairs.
  • Fixed clipping issues with the cape of ‘Hellion Armor’ when there are strong winds.
  • Fixed issues where PSSR was not properly enabled if the same account was used first on PS5 and then on PS5 Pro

Localization

  • Fixed incorrect localization of “Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced” on all platform packages in Simplified Chinese.
  • Fixed incorrect localization of the Trophy/Achievement “Ed the Diver” in Simplified Chinese.

Audio

  • Fixed various missing audio issues.
  • Fixed missing audio for when a normal guard blocked melee attacks from the player.
  • Fixed an issue where the Hideout’s watermill audio would be played after entering and exiting the menu despite the Hideout’s Garden not being unlocked.
  • Balanced certain dialogues in Simplified Chinese to be more audible.

SPOILERS AHEAD!

Quests

  • "Overrun and Outnumbered": Fixed an issue where James Kidd remained idle if the player skipped the cutscene and quickly used a “Sleep Dart” on an enemy.
  • “Delirium”: Fixed an issue where the sails could be seen floating when swimming up.
  • “Traveling Salesman”: Fixed an issue where low-quality civilian models could be observed if the player skipped through the cutscene.
  • “Vainglorious Bastards”: Fixed an issue where the “Royal African Ship” could sometimes sink after the cutscene.
  • “A Second Chance”: Fixed an issue where Edward could fast travel to the Jackdaw while carrying food, which may cause the food to disappear.
  • “Mayan Mysteries”: Fixed an issue where the “Mayan Armor” could not be obtained due to missing a Mayan stone that was obtained before “Overrun and Outnumbered” quest.
  • “A Cockalorum”: Lucy will sometimes go out of hiding during 'Reach the villa' objective.
  • “The Sage's buried secret”: Fixed an issue where James Kidd could get stuck if the player blocks his route up the rocks.
  • “What the Devil!”: Fixed an issue where players could unintentionally clear the objective “Board the HMS Demolition” as Edward.
  • “Templar Ships”: Fixed an issue where players could remain stuck in combat if they were detected by enemies while eavesdropping on civilians.
  • “Upton Travers”: Fixed an issue where the objective to ‘Kill Upton’ was missing after loading a save file.
  • “Diving for Medicines”: Fixed an issue where players could lose autosave files if they participate in “Uptown Travers” during the main quest.
  • Fixed an issue in certain quests where enemies did not react accordingly if inflicted by sleep/berserk dart while following another person.
  • Fixed an issue where on Black Island, "Morgan's Treasures" and "Midnight Moonshine" could sometimes remain unavailable to players.

https://www.gamingbible.com/news/baldurs.title: Baldur's Gate 3 drops surprise update that demands another playthrough, we're so back
https://www.gamingbible.com/news/baldurs.content:
Just when you think you’re finally done for good, Baldur’s Gate 3 finds yet another way to draw you back in.

Larian Studios’ hit 2023 TRPG has dropped a surprise update that surely demands yet another playthrough; after all, think of the narrative possibilities you’re yet to encounter.

Baldur’s Gate 3 now supports Xbox Play Anywhere with a free update dropping across all platforms in order to support this new feature.

If you’re not familiar with Xbox Play Anywhere, it essentially allows you to enjoy the same playthrough across Xbox, PC, and supported handhelds at no additional cost.

That means you could start Baldur’s Gate 3 on console at home before carrying on with your playthrough via a ROG Xbox Ally or Ally X during your commute or while on a weekend away.

So this update doesn’t necessarily change anything within the game, but that doesn’t mean you should disregard it if you’re of the impression that your time with Baldur’s Gate 3 is over.

As I said, there are likely tons of narrative possibilities you’re yet to encounter.

The only problem is that Baldur’s Gate 3 is a time consuming game and requires a fair bit of commitment, but just think how much easier it’s now going to be to embark on a playthrough with Xbox Play Anywhere enabled.

Fans seem to be pleased. “Thank you. Gives me an excuse to start a second playthrough on my Xbox Ally,” said one response to the announcement, echoing my own thoughts.

“Oh, I was waiting for a loooong time for this, thanks,” added another.

READ MORE: Baldur's Gate 3 'true' third-person mod makes it feel like a whole new game

Baldur’s Gate 4 is yet to find a studio with Larian working on Divinity

Unfortunately, we’re never actually going to see any true new content for Baldur’s Gate 3 - outside of the world of modding anyway.

That’s because Larian Studios is now working on a new instalment in the Divinity series, simply titled Divinity.

It’s believed to be somewhat of a soft reboot, almost like God of War (2018) was for Santa Monica’s IP; Divinity isn’t expected to override the existing canon, but it should act as the perfect step into the franchise for newbies.

The title was revealed at 2025 The Game Awards with a very gory cinematic trailer after Larian set up a mysterious hell statue in the Californian desert.

Divinity will be a turn-based RPG so it should still appeal to those who like Baldur’s Gate 3’s general formula; single-player and multiplayer options are expected to be included.

As for the future of the Baldur’s Gate franchise, that remains up in the air.

Wizards of the Coast owns the rights for a potential ‘Baldur’s Gate 4’ and hopes for it to be made, but hasn’t currently optioned them to a studio.

Wizards of the Coast-owned studio Invoke is, however, creating Warlock - a third-person single-player action-adventure set within the Dungeons & Dragons universe.

Little has been shown of the game beyond a cinematic trailer but we know that it’s slated to land in 2027 on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC.

It could be one to watch if you’re mourning the absence of Baldur’s Gate - and, of course, there’s HBO’s Baldur’s Gate TV show in development which could bring back some original cast members from the recent game.

https://www.gamingbible.com/news/tv-and-.title: Dave Bautista in talks for GoW adaptation, but not the one he was campaigning for
https://www.gamingbible.com/news/tv-and-.content:
Dave Bautista is reported to be in talks for a role in a ‘GoW’ adaptation, but just not the one he was originally campaigning for.

The Guardians of the Galaxy star has been attached to a Gears of War movie since at least 2018, expressing on several occasions how he’s wanted to play Marcus Fenix in live-action form.

But now it’s reported that he’s now in talks to star in a slightly different ‘GoW’ adaptation, apparently being cast to take over as Kratos in Amazon Prime Video’s God of War television series.

As reported by Variety, Bautista is in talks to take over from original lead star Ryan Hurst following the actor’s injury on set.

Hurst was cast in January 2026, but had to leave the project in June following a torn bicep injury he received on set. The decision was then made to recast the lead role, despite four episodes already being filmed.

What followed was weeks of speculation regarding which actor could tackle the role next, with rumours telling of WWE star Braun Strowman in possible talks to join the series.

Read More: God of War TV show gets another recast update as Season 2 plans revealed

Dave Bautista finally could get his perfect GoW role

We reckon Bautista is a good bet for this role though. The role of Kratos demands an impressive muscular physique, something that would be difficult for any actor to prepare for on short notice.

Bautista, however, has been in good physical shape throughout his entire career, from his early days as a wrestler to his role in the Marvel Cinematic Universe as Drax the Destroyer.

Aside from this though, we also believe Bautista has the emotional gravitas to play the more sensitive side of Kratos as well. Having the character be this incredibly large, muscular force of nature is one thing, but Kratos’ quieter, more reflective moments are what makes him such an interesting character.

The actor had previously stated on numerous occasions that playing Marcus Fenix in a live-action Gears of War game would be a “dream role”, so it’ll be interesting to see how he slides into this other ‘GoW’ role if he’s selected.

“I’ve been pursuing Gears of War for years now. I believe it’s in the hands of Universal Studios. And I’ve been knocking on their door and badgering them and they are so sick of me (laughs), phoning in and asking them where they are with that project. But, yes, Marcus Fenix is absolutely a dream role for me. I want that role.”

After making a name for himself in wrestling since 1999, Bautista grew his fame as an actor in the 2010s after becoming known for playing Drax the Destroyer in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, most notably the Guardians of the Galaxy trilogy.

He has also played big roles in films like Zack Snyder’s Army of the Dead, Blade Runner 2049, Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery, and Spectre.

https://www.gamingbible.com/news/platfor.title: Free 3-month subscription to Xbox Game Pass is easy to claim; see if you're eligible
https://www.gamingbible.com/news/platfor.content:
Free subscriptions to Xbox Game Pass are being handed out thanks to the service’s latest collaboration, but only a select few will be eligible to claim.

While all of the current gaming subscription services have their flaws, Xbox Game Pass stands as the objective best of the bunch. It’s not perfect, but with so many day-one first-party exclusives like Halo: Campaign Evolved it at least makes tiers like Ultimate worth the extra money.

Those who are yet to experience the pleasures of Game Pass, however, can now do so with a new offer from Discord; or more specifically NVIDIA.

Through the NVIDIA App gamers can claim a three-month subscription to Discord Nitro, which now comes bundled with an Xbox Game Pass Starter subscription.

To claim, all you need to do is set up a NVIDIA account if you don’t have one already, launch the app, log in and redeem your membership. It couldn’t be simpler.

The only problem is this offer won’t be available to everyone. The offer is aimed at new subscribers to Discord Nitro, so if you currently have a membership or have had one in the last 12 months, you won’t be eligible.

Nevertheless, it’s a decent offer for those yet to give it a go, though you should only be claiming for the free Xbox Game Pass. Discord Nitro is notoriously hated as it locks basic features behind a paywall.

However, Nitro is also one of the ways you’ll get to play Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 (2026) early if that adds any incentive at all…

READ NEXT: Call of Duty on Xbox Game Pass expertly highlights why the service is so brilliant

What’s included in the Xbox Game Pass Starter subscription?

Like we said before, Xbox Game Pass Starter is an entry-level membership intended to give you a taste of what the larger Game Pass subscriptions can offer.

You get access to 50 titles such Ori and the Will of the Wisps, DOOM Eternal, The Elder Scrolls Online: Standard Edition, and Fallout 4.

There's 10 hours of Cloud Streaming each month offered for those that don’t like having to install their games.

As expected, it’s a very basic offering, and unfortunately it misses one of the biggest inclusions of all: online multiplayer. For whatever reason, this was omitted from the tier so unless you’re playing a free-to-play online game like Fortnite, you won’t be able to play with friends.

All in all, this special offer is fine. The obvious problem is it’s only available for those who haven’t been subscribed to Discord Nitro, either ever or over the last 12 months. With the amount of free memberships the service has doled out over the years that’s bound to be a very small number of gamers, so thousands of people will be ineligible for this deal.

For those who haven’t had memberships though, this is worth a go, especially if you fancy playing 50 free games and don’t care about online multiplayer.

READ NEXT: Xbox reveals slew of free gifts to users as 25 years celebration continues

https://www.gamingbible.com/news/platfor.title: Pokémon Pokopia free 2.0 update fixes infuriating issue with new feature
https://www.gamingbible.com/news/platfor.content:
It’s a bountiful day for players of Pokémon Pokopia as today, 4 August, marks the arrival of both phase one of the game’s paid DLC and its free 2.0 update.

The former, Bubbly Basin, can be obtained as part of Pokémon Pokopia’s paid expansion pass which is due to drop in three phases.

Bubbly Basin, a new underwater biome, lands today. The second phase is said to add “additional new features” with a release date listed of 31 March 2027 when pre-ordering.

Phase three will introduce another new town with a current planned launch date of 30 September 2027.

These dates are to be taken with a pinch of salt as phase two has been marketed as “late 2026” by Nintendo, so these are likely placeholders.

The expansion pass will set you back £29.99 / $34.99 but if you don’t want to splash the cash, you can enjoy Pokémon Pokopia’s free new 2.0 update.

It introduces a new item that’ll fix what is easily the game’s biggest (and perhaps only) issue, storage.

Pokémon Pokopia’s new shared storage chest will finally stop you losing your items

Pokémon Pokopia offers you tons of items, especially if you’re into landscaping and acquire huge swathes of blocks.

The problem is that your inventory only carries so much, so the player is forced to rely on storage chests.

That too is a problem though as storage chests also have limitations; you’ll need plenty of them and only the four placed directly connecting to a crafting bench will allow you to pull materials from them when crafting.

However, if you need a furniture or food item or such like, it’s so easy to forget what storage chest you put it in and in which town.

Losing items within your storage is a common problem that plagues most Pokémon Pokopia players, but you needn’t worry anymore as the 2.0 update is set to introduce a shared storage chest.

As reported by Famitsu, the chest has 140 slots which vastly outnumbers the current maximum chest size of 60 slots.

Most significantly though, this specific type of chest can have its contents accessed from all of the game’s various towns or biomes so opening it up in, say, the Withered Wasteland will show you the same items as you’ll find opening it up in Bleak Beach.

This is going to be perfect for storing your most important building items that you want to access across all parts of the game.

It was also detailed that the free update will include the new dive mechanic, allowing players to pick up underwater loot, ‘frameless glass’, and a new underwater electricity generator.

READ MORE: Pokémon Gen 10 leak confirms the franchise's biggest Pokédex total so far

Bubbly Basin introduces a ton of new ‘mon to the game’s Pokédex

As for what you can expect in paid expansion Bubbly Basin, Serebii.net notes that the area will introduce a new Pokédex with Wiglett, Mareanie, Golisopod, Stunfisk, and Sharpedo all expected to appear.

All current skills will work underwater with surf set to receive some kind of boost.

It’s interesting to note that this probably won’t be Pokémon Pokopia’s only expansion pass.

A prior leak confirmed five additional towns, none of which were featured in the game at launch. They are as follows:

  • Viridian area with a “never ending burning forest of ash”.
  • Cerulean area with “a flooded city that has hidden treasure”.
  • Cinnibar area with a “forever sealed dead volcano island”.
  • Lavender area with a “rotten tower that reaches heaven”.
  • Caledeon area with “a giant crater that reaches unseeable depth”.

The Cerulean area is clearly Bubbly Basin with another one of these towns likely being the focus of the third phase of this current expansion.

That still leaves three towns left to add, however. There is the possibility that developers could drop a new town for free but that feels less likely.

For now though, we have both Bubbly Basin and the 2.0 update to enjoy - and I suppose it’s about time that I actually got back to tidying up my biomes after a few weeks of neglect.

https://www.gamingbible.com/news/2026-an.title: 2026's best 10/10 Animal Crossing cozy rival confirms PS5 and Switch 2 ports
https://www.gamingbible.com/news/2026-an.content:
While Pokémon Pokopia will arguably go down as 2026’s very best cozy offering, it’s an entirely different kettle of fish to what’s on offer in life sims like Animal Crossing: New Horizons and Stardew Valley.

If you’re after something new and of that specific cozy ilk, then Starsand Island is 2026’s standout offering - and it’s finally coming to PlayStation 5 and Nintendo Switch 2.

Starsand Island originally launched in early access in February of this year on PC and Xbox, garnering a perfect score of 10 out of 10 from us here at GAMINGbible.

It now nears its exciting 1.0 launch which’ll bring new content to the game with developer Seed Sparkle Lab also having announced long-awaited PlayStation 5 and Nintendo Switch 2 ports.

Both the new content and new ports will launch on August 18 which is mere weeks away.

If this is the first you’re hearing of Starsand Island, this life sim sees you abandon your miserable, fast-paced life in the city.

Instead, you’ll return to an island that you used to call home, connecting with old friends, and re-evaluating the joys of life.

It includes all of the usual cozy fare, including farming, fishing, decorating, gardening, raising animals, romancing, and more.

With its open-world exploration, light combat, and varied terrain and build customisation options, Starsand Island also has a The Sims or Zelda feel to it in parts.

READ MORE: 13 upcoming 2026 cozy games to wishlist if you're sick of farming

Every new feature in Starsand Island’s 1.0 launch

The 1.0 launch will introduce online multiplayer so you can enjoy the sights and sounds of Starsand Island alongside three friends.

Partaking in multiplayer play earns you unique currency you can use for exclusive rewards in a multiplayer shop.

Relationship options are also set to be expanded with 19 NPCs now boasting three-heart and five-heart relationship quests.

There remain 14 romance options but those characters have gained new dating activities, including picnics, kite flying, and playing arcade games.

Developers are also adding an Autumn Pumpkin Festival which will boast its own storyline and quests.

Starsand Island’s players will also get to enjoy limited-time events like catching glowing jellyfish, growing festival pumpkins, and providing animals with special feed to produce candy.

Taking part in the festivities unlocks exclusive rewards including outfits, emotes, recipes, and more.

If you don’t yet own Starsand Island, both the PlayStation 5 and Nintendo Switch 2 versions are set to launch at £39.99 / $39.99 / €44.99.

Again, the game earned a perfect score of 10 from us here at GAMINGbible.

“Starsand Island is exactly what I’ve claimed it to be in previous previews. It’s the very best of Animal Crossing, Stardew Valley, and The Sims, with a flavouring of Studio Ghibli thrown in, but it’s also something completely original,” we said.

“Starsand Island’s depth of offering places it leagues above its competitors making it, for me, the new poster child of the cosy gaming space. I’ll be championing it until the rest of the world catches on, but I have a feeling that won’t take very long.”

https://www.gamingbible.com/news/tainted.title: Skyrim-inspired 2025 RPG gets new free DLC with 98% positive ratings
https://www.gamingbible.com/news/tainted.content:
Tainted Grail: The Fall of Avalon players can now pick up a free DLC which adds a load of new content.

The 2025 RPG that was heavily inspired by The Elder Scrolls has been a smash hit with players, charting several thousand players each day that has remained steady over the past year since hitting its 1.0 release.

In the past 12 months, the game has received a large paid expansion, as well as several smaller free DLCs. Most notably, there have been several free DLCs labelled “Bonus Content”.

The latest free DLC to come to Tainted Grail is the fourth Bonus Content pack, released towards the end of July, which adds plenty of new free content to the game.

Bonus Content #4 adds some deadly new tools for players who favour bows and sorcery, with brand new playstyles and unique items to select in your arsenal.

As expected, the DLC adds some new bows and wands, giving you more ways to approach ranged combat and spellcasting. In total, there are seven new bows to collect, and five new wands added.

Most notably, you get the brand new Scalesong Set, a selection of armour pieces which are useful for players using archery. Some bonuses included here offer you increased ranged damage, as well as reduced damage while aiming a bow and reduced bow draw time.

If you’re a mage on the other hand, you get the new Dolorous Pilgrim Set. This is made for magic wielders who draw power from bloodletting, pain, and self-sacrifice. Some of the bonuses in this set include being able to increase health, applying new effects to your attacks, and increasing your mana.

Tainted Grail: The Fall of Avalon has been well received by most players since launch

All of this new equipment can be purchased from blacksmiths, but also be found during Wyrdnight as unidentified loot waiting to be discovered by players.

Meanwhile, this new free DLC also features a brand new romance option as an extra. Buying the house in Cuanacht now opens up a romance path with your new neighbour, who has taken an interest in you.

Although the new additions are minimal, the release has also been received positively by Tainted Grail players. As of writing, the Steam reviews currently give the DLC a positive rating of 98% recommendations. If you're unfamiliar with how percentages work, that's pretty high.

“Damn more free DLC?! Way to go Devs!!!!,” reads one review from a player.

“Awesome. Waiting for the next paid DLC. After all of those freebies and continuous support I would buy the next DLC without even seeing what's inside. In this day and age finding developers that care about their game is a unicorn; and it shows,” reads another positive review.

If you want to check out the new content added to Tainted Grail: The Fall of Avalon, you can download it now from Steam.

Read More: Skyrim gets free 'DLC Scale' Zelda expansion

https://www.gamingbible.com/news/platfor.title: Players go wild for free Game Pass extraction fantasy title that combines Elden Ring and Arc Raiders
https://www.gamingbible.com/news/platfor.content:
So far, the extraction genre has been monopolised by guns and bullets.

Unloading looted lead in Escape from Tarkov, Call of Duty's DMZ mode, and ARC Raiders have been the only way to enjoy the grindable, scalable, enjoyable take on a multiplayer PvPvE experience.

Yet what happens when you take that blueprint and sprinkle in a bit of soulslike, Elden Ring-esque combat, trading a 50. cal for a greatsword or battleaxe?

Well, that's the recipe for Mistfall Hunter, and this fantasy extraction is everything we could have hoped for.

Free on Xbox Game Pass or £20 on Steam (thanks to a small discount), Mistfall Hunters has players going bananas.

Mistfall Hunter 'scratches that itch' of a fantasy extraction dream

Having become the home of multiplayer shooters, Xbox Game Pass has recently begun championing more titles than its typical franchises like Gears of War: E-Day.

With one foot in the fantasy door - carried by The Elder Scrolls - the perfect blend of their two loves has now landed in the lap of the Game Pass, and straight off the bat, Mistfall Hunter has impressed.

Described as 'a dark fantasy extraction ARPG', Mistfall Hunter plunges players into a 'forbidden realm consumed by the mist.'

"Caught in a ruthless loop of high-stakes looting, deadly combat, and desperate extractions, you must fight for your life in the shadows to experience the ultimate dark fantasy survival test," reads the description.

Whether you're running solo or with a small band of rebels, the objective is to loot as much gear that complements your character type, fight enemy squads with blades or arcane arts, escape the realm with your bounty, and gear up for the next run to continue growing.

Read Next: Xbox Game Pass action freebie is a must-play if you loved The Odyssey

With endless build possibilities, the new take on the extraction genre has been applauded, despite some slight performance woes on high-end PCs.

"I was really craving an extraction game that didn’t revolve around guns, and there just aren’t many options out there. Mistfall Hunter scratches that itch," one glowing review reads.

"The art style is clearly inspired by Elden Ring, but don’t go in expecting it to play like it — this is very much its own thing."

A second player wrote, "I'm really enjoying the game. The combat is interesting, feels good and easy to pick up. Graphics are nice and the map design is interesting with lots of levels."

Even those buying the game off Steam have enjoyed it, despite complaints of frame drops on the platform.

"A brilliant blend of many other successful titles. If you would enjoy a less punishing version of Dark and Darker with the combat of Elden Ring, this is for you. Worth every penny," another reviewer said.

A second Steam purchaser added, "Gameplay feels like a great balance of approachability while also having a high skill ceiling potential on all the classes. Have seen some people complaining about balancing issues, but every fight I have lost I feel there were multiple mistakes or things I could have done differently to come out on top. Don't listen to the haters! For $25, this game is an absolute steal!"

Many comments said the drops aren't as big of an issue as people have claimed, too, which seems to be the only complaint.

"I had some lag with the Game Pass version but the Steam one runs perfectly fine. The game is quite fun if you got 1-2 friends to sign up with," another said.

https://www.gamingbible.com/news/fallout.title: Fallout: New California is now one click away and the best New Vegas spin-off you could ask for
https://www.gamingbible.com/news/fallout.content:
Fallout: New Vegas is getting an official remaster, that much we know, but many fans still hope for a full-on sequel one day.

Unfortunately it’s not looking likely. Fallout 5 will presumably be the next mainline entry in the series and any future spin-offs will probably be set in new locations, rather than dredging up places from the past.

At least we’re returning to both Washington D.C and New Vegas in those confirmed Fallout 3 and Fallout: New Vegas remasters though.

Those that want a full-on sequel however have sort of got one already; Fallout- New California.

Fallout- New California is a free expansion mod for Fallout: New Vegas. It’s also the biggest one yet.

It’s a completely new story that’s playable from start to finish, packing almost 25 hours of new content if you want to be a completionist.

New California’s story synopsis reads: “Vault 18 is at the heart of the California Wasteland high in the San Bernardino Mountains, and its legendary Wasteland Scouts have managed to keep its secrets safe for decades despite the wars raging beyond the great door. In their old age, the Scouts have created a new generation to take their place... if their rebellious adopted kids survive the Enclave threat brewing within their own ranks.”

The New California Republic makes a return, and if you’re looking for more NCR-focused quests we’d also recommend checking out the Long 15 expansion mod too.

All of the mod’s quests are fully-voice acted and you’ll even get access to two new radio stations, which is easily one of the best parts of any Fallout game provided the best songs aren’t ripped from the game’s soundtrack.

Previously New California was obtainable via NexusMods, but now it’s made its way to GOG as a one-click installation, provided you’ve got a copy of Fallout: New Vegas of course. If you don’t it’s currently 60% off for those living in the United Kingdom.

READ NEXT: 5 changes Bethesda we'd like to see in the Fallout: New Vegas remaster

GOG’s ‘One-Click Mods’ were introduced back in June 2025, and is a quick-and-simple method of enhancing your games so long as their supported by the platform.

GOG and the future of gaming

Over the past few years GOG has been making some of the best moves in the game industry, and while it’s yet to reach the same heights of success as Steam it’s still a well-respected, and well-trusted, online outlet.

Earlier this year PlayStation announced it’d be ending support of physical media in the year of our Lord 2028, and it kicked up a real fuss about the future of discs.

GOG has an answer to this though as one of its free tools lets you easily burn a copy of your digital game to a disc for future preservation.

It also regularly tracks down and relists games you can’t find on modern platforms, which is great news for retro enthusiasts.

READ NEXT: GOG interview: Sending private detectives, landing white whales, and preserving classic games

https://www.gamingbible.com/news/platfor.title: Free 10/10 Steam game lands as gorgeous pixel art screams Game Boy nostalgia
https://www.gamingbible.com/news/platfor.content:
A brand new free game has landed on Steam, sporting gorgeous pixel art and huge amounts of nostalgia.

One of the main benefits of glancing through Steam’s free offerings is it’s great for when your budget for new games has hit too low.

There’s almost always something that looks pretty decent when you look at the new free games coming to Steam each week, and this new retro-style game from developer Red Studio looks to be the case here.

Titled Avoidvania, this new free game on Steam is described as a “top-down runner” and metroidvania played from a 2D perspective.

Taking place in a world that is a mix of medieval and fantasy, Avoidvania has you play as a small cat who walks into a forest and smells an “irresistible aroma coming from the tower of a large castle”.

Following the smell, you become trapped inside a maze of corridors and rooms which are laden with traps, as well as hostile creatures out to get you.

As a cat, you’re unable to fight with your small body, but you do have the advantage of being able to outrun them very quickly. You can also get help from other travellers who have made it to this strange place.

Read More: Hysterical Steam freebie goes viral with 97% positive rating, perfect for weekend co-op

Avoidvania was previously a paid game released in 2021, but is now available for all players to play for free

Previously a paid game released in 2021, Avoidvania has now been made permanently free this week in a recent update. It has also clarified that refunds are available if the game was purchased recently.

“Avoidvania is going permanently free on Steam by the end of July,” reads a statement by Red Studio.

“The validation process with Steam is underway, we'll confirm as soon as it's live. The game will remain as it is: unfortunately, funding didn't come through. If you purchased it recently, Steam refunds are still available. Thank you for your support, and we hope to see you on future projects!”

Although it only has 11 user reviews on Steam, every review posted for the game has been recommended so far which has led to a 100% positive review score.

One user review reads: “Avoidvania has a ton of places to explore and the achievements are really tough to get. I'm impressed.”

Meanwhile, another positive review states “It's not very long and a different style of Metroidvania games. Overall I enjoyed playing the game. Trying to avoid enemies traps and other hazards is simplistic but still offers some challenge.”

Altogether, it seems like a pretty interesting game to get to grips with. The fact that it’s free and has low system requirements is a plus as well, as there isn’t much stopping you from checking it out except for time.

You can download Avoidvania to play now from Steam.

Read More: Steam free taster is Silent Hill meets Twin Peaks and the best metroidvania we've played all year

https://www.gamingbible.com/news/save-ga.title: You can now save the gaming devs with new 150-game collection for just $10
https://www.gamingbible.com/news/save-ga.content:
The gaming industry is full of super-talented developers who have felt the cold hardship of mass layoffs.

Just recently, Xbox announced it was culling many of its studios to put stock back into its major franchises, with a repored 4,000 jobs at risk over the year, and an initial 1,600 roles being made redundant - that's the second major cutback from Microsoft's gaming division in two years, leaving games to be cancelled in the wake of the purge.

In the last two years alone, giants like Sony (and Bungie), Take-Two Interactive, Ubisoft, and EA have all cut down on their staff size, leaving many devoted devs without work.

According to the Game Industry Hardship Fund, around 33 percent of developers have been impacted by layoffs in the last two years, with the post-pandemic gaming boom reeling back to normality and an increased reliance on AI.

But in a bid to support these out-of-work people, a new initiative from the Game Industry Hardship Fund has been created, raising $100,000 through an awesome indie game bundle with just shy of 150 titles to choose from.

You too can enjoy this massive collection of cool games, saving 99% on individual titles, with funds being invested straight back into the clever minds that brought you the biggest AAA games of the modern generation.

Read Next: 10 promising indie games that could rival AAAs in the remainder of 2026

$10 Game industry hardship fund bundle includes some awesome surprises

For as much as your coffee and croissant round on a daily commute, a new bundle on itch.io offers nearly 150 indie games that would usually cost $5-10 themselves on Steam or Windows.

With endless hours of gameplay to crawl through, some highlights include the likes of Winter Witch, a cozy fantasy exploration title with a cute cat for company; A Short Hike, a quippy adventure title putting you in the shoes of a flying penguin, scoring Steam's coveted 'overwhelmingly positive' rating; and Psychroma, a psychological horror side-scroller set in a haunted cyberpunk house.

Other popular choices in the bundle include Lucah: Born of a Dream, Arranger, Eldritch, and Cook, Serve, Delicious!

The $10 offer only lasts for ten more days, though, meaning you only have a limited time to finish what you're playing and carve out some time for cutesy indie action.

All funds will go to the United Videogame Workers scheme, which supports developers in the US and Canada who have been hit with hardship.

The fund will remain open long after the 150 game collection offer expires, but who wouldn't want a cheap collection of titles for as much as a pint and a packet of chips?

https://www.gamingbible.com/news/elden-r.title: Elden Ring DLC rumours abuzz following FromSoftware's cryptic social media activity
https://www.gamingbible.com/news/elden-r.content:
It's been two long years since Elden Ring's last expansion, and players refuse to believe that FromSoftware is done with the wildly captivating fantasy realm it created.

Although the base game is entering its Bloodborne and Skyrim arc, being a legacy RPG that continues to surprise fans with secrets only now being uncovered, Elden Ring has a lot more to give.

Yet it has been two years since Shadow of the Erdtree was dropped as the ultimate 'send-off', described in our review as "a fitting conclusion to FromSoftware’s biggest, and most successful title to date."

Despite FromSoftware cooking up the online multiplayer spin-off Nightreign in May last year, and the clear 'ending' that the Shadow of the Erdtree brought, fans of the fantasy realm still want more from this award-winning title.

Now, activity on the developers' social media page has sent the community into a frenzy, with many people claiming that a new Elden Ring DLC could be on the way.

Elden Ring fans convinced of a second DLC after recent X posts

Hot on the back of Elden Ring's success, FromSoftware has been devoted to bringing players the 'next' Bloodborne, with The Duskbloods landing on Nintendo Switch 2 as the developers' ambitious spiritual successor.

Yet it's clear that there is still love for Elden Ring, as new posts on X (previously Twitter) showcased some new content that players are now convinced ties directly into a Godwyn DLC.

The inconspicuous post appeared to be harmless at first watch, but the 12-second video has now amassed over 6.5 million views, as those fans who have been waiting for years for more content have come to some interesting conclusions.

Even the perilous hunt for the demigods holds moments of quiet wonder.#ELDENRING pic.twitter.com/5sJyVOYi17

— ELDEN RING (@ELDENRING) July 31, 2026

All the video shows is a quick pony ride through the Siofra River, as a lack of giant crab and Ancestral Follower enemies made for a 'quiet wonder'.

But it is a different type of post from what we usually see the developers release, and highlights new skins for Torrent that are quickly being construed as a hype-building device for a new expansion.

Read Next: 7 Essential Elden Ring Mods Which Offer A Brand New Challenge

Spinning social media into a mass craze, players are fuelled on copium.

"FROMSOFT RELEASE GODWYN DLC AND MY LIFE IS YOURS," reads the top comment on the post.

A second said, "HUNT for the DEMIGODS > shows empty Siofra River > one way to get to Deeproot Depths is through the Siofra Aqueduct and transporter coffin > GODWYN DLC ?????"

"I am delusional please give me a second expansion," a third person said.

Yet there is more Elden Ring content on the way that wouldn't relate to a Godwyn DLC.

Others have theorised that this could be the first piece of marketing material for the live-action film, which wrapped up filming last week. It could also be tied to the upcoming Nintendo Switch 2 Tarnished Edition, which comes this month.

Still, there's no ruling out that the theories are true...

In the meantime, though, fan-made mods are now producing mass DLC-sized expansions, such as The Convergence, which are essential playthroughs for all Elden Ring fans.

That can fill some void, although an official DLC would be best.

https://www.gamingbible.com/news/tv-and-.title: Surprise free Batman game launches, adapts fan-favourite TV show
https://www.gamingbible.com/news/tv-and-.content:
It’s not everyday that we’re surprised with a new Batman game, let alone one that’s free.

That’s precisely what’s happened though, with Batman: Caped Crusader - Chronicles having launched on Amazon Luna, formerly Prime Gaming.

Amazon Luna is Amazon’s free gaming service included within the price of all standard Prime memberships.

Typically, Amazon Luna only offers PC titles but what’s wonderful about Batman: Caped Crusader - Chronicles is that it doesn’t require a PC, console, or controller; it can be enjoyed directly from the Prime app with Fire TV in the US and UK or on compatible smartphones.

The game was launched to celebrate the arrival of Batman: Caped Crusader’s second season, following on from the series’ acclaimed initial outing in 2024.

The well-received animated series offers a 1940s take on the classic Batman story, with Season 2 currently boasting a 90% score on Rotten Tomatoes.

READ MORE: Batman Gotham by Gaslight footage resurfaces as Arkham-like game you'll never get to play

Step into the shoes of a GCPD investigator in Batman: Caped Crusader - Chronicles

As for the surprise free game Batman: Caped Crusader - Chronicles, it loosely adapts the series, allowing fans to step into the shoes of a GCPD investigator.

You’ll team up with Batman and Detective Montoya to solve a number of perplexing cases.

“Team up with up to three friends to investigate 11 episodic cases, uncover clues through unique detective-themed minigames, and bring notorious villains like Scarecrow, Babyface, and The Joker to justice,” teased a press release.

Batman: Caped Crusader’s cast reprise their roles with Hamish Linklater as Batman, Michelle C. Bonilla as Detective Montoya, and the newly announced Matthew Needham as The Joker.

If you don’t have a Fire TV, you can also enjoy Batman: Caped Crusader - Chronicles via other compatible devices like smartphones or laptops.

You should expect the same quality of animation for portions of the game. Players are able to select between Story Mode or Quickplay with the latter allowing you to choose to replay your favourite missions.

When playing on a TV, your smartphone will act as your controller. Players can speak into their phone during interviews, trying their best to get suspects to open up.

You’ll also need to piece together destroyed evidence, search crime scenes for clues, decode witness statements, diffuse bombs, and more.

It’s definitely one for puzzle fans. You can take a look at what the game has to offer below.

Fans were, unsurprisingly, pretty hyped by the unexpected reveal.

“Huh, actually looks pretty fun,” said one trailer viewer. “Woohoo! Looks great. Can’t wait to play this after work,” added another.

Someone simply declared: “Masterpiece.”

As for Season 2 of Batman: Caped Crusader, it’s out now on Prime Video and consists of 10 episodes with all episodes having dropped in one go.

The series is yet to be renewed for a third season with that likely relying on viewership numbers for the newly released Season 2 so if you care about the show’s future, you better get watching.

We have seen numerous reports about Chinese memory giant CXMT and its production. According to multiple reports, CXMT's LPDDR6 memory will operate at speeds of up to 12.8 Gbps, with the base speed of LPDDR6 being 10.7 Gbps. LPDDR6 picks up where LPDDR5X left off, which could reach speeds of up to 10.7 Gbps when highly overclocked. However, the newest standard is pushing for much higher speeds, with the first generation of LPDDR6 from CXMT's fabs reaching 12.8 Gbps. Additionally, CXMT is producing these chips with a 16 Gb capacity, equivalent to 2 GB, and the memory IC is placed inside a package-on-package (POP) casing, featuring about 1,295 pins in a ball grid array.

For now, this production will be only a trial run before high-volume manufacturing (HVM), which will likely take place weeks or even months after the initial risk production. Currently, the company is shipping its LPDDR6 to customers for validation, suggesting that we will likely see full risk production soon. As CXMT has manufacturing, construction, and other factors far ahead of industry standards, it is possible that HVM will occur in just a few weeks.

https://www.techpowerup.com/351344/memor.content:
According to DigiTimes, industry insiders are now claiming that the entire memory production capacity for 2027 has been fully booked, well ahead of the schedule the industry expected. All of the big three memory makers—Samsung, SK hynix, and Micron—have sold out their memory capacity for the upcoming year, leaving no room for additional supply for third parties to purchase more DRAM wafers. Interestingly, the report notes that everyone from OEM server makers and PC makers to AI labs knows that July and August are crucial months for securing allocations for the following year. However, some businesses have been kept in the dark because nobody has been public about this out of fear of losing their allocation.

Memory makers have been pushing customers into long-term agreements with contracts ranging from three to five years, using an advance payment deposit model where customers essentially pre-pay for some of the memory capacity. These deals are made on an individual customer level. All of this combined signals that 2027 will be the worst year in recent history regarding memory shortages, meaning that only those who managed to sign agreements for supply will benefit, while the rest are left without as there simply isn't enough available DRAM. Only about 60-70% of the estimated demand can be met in 2027, leaving a significant amount of demand unmet and waiting for the 2028 supply.

https://www.ign.com/articles/mr-trippy-a.content:
Developer Silver Bullet has announced Mr Trippy, a new management sim where, at first glance, it seems like you're running an ice cream truck. And you are! Except, that's not all you're pushing. Some of your clientele will also come looking for treats that hit a little harder than a soft-serve vanilla cone. Something like, I don't know...meth.

Yes, you'll live a double life in your ice cream truck, looking legit on the outside while pushing seriously illicit stuff inside the truck's doors. You'll have to learn the patterns of the watchful cops, evading them and keeping your Heat Meter low. As you become a bigger and bigger dealer, you'll upgrade and customize your beat-up truck and expand your territory into new neighborhoods. You'll also have to learn to launder your money through local businesses, lest the cops (and/or the tax man) catch onto you.

Check out the first trailer and screenshots above, and wishlist Mr Trippy on Steam if you're interested.

https://www.ign.com/articles/fire-emblem.title: Everything Announced in The Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave Nintendo Direct
https://www.ign.com/articles/fire-emblem.content:
We've rounded up everything announced in today's Nintendo Direct broadcast focused on Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, including a big reveal of the game's true protagonist, several big choices and some heroic timey-wimey shenanigans.

Today's broadcast featured 20 minutes of new details for Nintendo's upcoming Switch 2 exclusive, which is set to launch in just over a month on September 17.

Fortune's Weave is the first major launch in Nintendo's beloved RPG franchise for several years, and looks to once again embrace the gameplay that made 2019's Fire Emblem: Three Houses so successful. After a so-so successor in Fire Emblem: Engage, this new title looks to very much be a Three Houses sequel, with the return of Heroes' Relics and Crests, and a familiar face in an older Sothis.

As ever, Fortune's Weave will feature the Fire Emblem series' familiar turn-based gameplay and colorful characters, this time set in and around an enormous arena, site of a championship named the Heroic Games. Read on for all the new details!

Four Character Stories to Choose From

Fortune's Weave is set in The Dagda Empire, 1449, and in the capital city of Dagison — a bustling hub, which is where the Heroic Games take place in a Roman-style amphitheature. On offer is a worthy prize: the granting of one wish from Dagda's ruler Solel.

Each of the game's four heroes offer their own storyline and set of allies:

  • Cai is a young farm boy looking to save his imprisoned father.
  • Dietrich is a brooding seafarer attacked by an enormous monster, washed ashore and seeking glory.
  • Theodora is seeking to win to restore peace to her remote home kingdom that worships a mysterious goddess.
  • Leda is a young woman born into prestige but who becomes consumed by rage at her father's murder. She learns that the killer's plan is to participate in the games.

There's Plenty of City Activities Outside Battle

Beyond fighting in the arena, there's plenty to do before you prep for your next scrap. Once a week training is available at the arena to level up your fighters. Here, you can also watch battles between your opponents to gather useful intel on their techniques. The shopping arcade, meanwhile, will let you enhance your weapons.

A temple will allow you to receive a blessing, which provides stat buffs in battle. Certification Exams let you try to obtain different classes for your characters. Townsfolk quests are also available to complete for rewards. And you can recruit powerful warriors, who may try and turn you away at first. Luckily, you can try again after winning them over — either by giving them gifts or taking them to dinner.

Inns allow you to rest and recharge, and also receive materials automatically over time. It's here that you'll engage in conversations with your support characters. (And yes, we did get a glimpse at a bathhouse scene.)

One final, mysterious location was also shown: the Pale Raven's Perch. Using the powers of this mysterious bird, you can swap to one of the other heroes, allowing you to play through all four characters in parallel!

Adventure Further Afield via The World Map

Exploration beyond the city of Dagison is possible, with overworld skirmishes against bandits and dungeon exploration. But time will pass as you explore, inevitably calling you back to the arena once more.

One major reveal here was regular turn-based combat in dungeons, rather than the grid-based battles the series is known for. These battles will let you combo attacks with support allies, and all four characters will offer their own unique abilities. Dungeons will also allow you to collect materials and other items.

The Story Continues, Five Years Later

After a time jump, Fortune's Weave will reveal its main protagonist, Eshmel, a hero who must stop the destruction of Dagda in 1454. Yes, those four characters earlier were merely the introduction!

Playing as Eshmel, you are called down by Sothis to try and save the kingdom. And it's here that Fortune's Weave will give players another big choice: to save the kingdom solo, or bring the game's earlier four heroes to the future to help in your quest, aided by the time-travelling powers of goddess Fortuna.

More to follow...

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

https://www.ign.com/articles/spider-man-.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day's 'Small Potatoes' Stakes Might Just Be the Solution to Superhero Fatigue
https://www.ign.com/articles/spider-man-.content:
With apologies to the excellent and beloved Captain America movies, my favorite character series within the greater MCU is unquestionably Tom Holland’s Spider-Man films. And as the box office results show, I’m clearly not alone. Like seemingly most of the rest of the world, I went to see Spider-Man: Brand New Day at my local movie theater this past weekend. Though I’ve loved all three of the previous Spidey films and expected to enjoy this one, I still couldn’t help but feel a bit less enthusiastic heading into it on account of the same superhero movie fatigue that a lot of my fellow moviegoers seem to be experiencing these days. It just hasn’t been the same since Endgame.

By the time Brand New Day’s credits (and post-credits scene) rolled, however, I was left in shock at just how much I adored the fourth Spider-Man film. It’s rare enough for a superhero series to sustain excellence for three movies, let alone four – heck, even Iron Man himself, Robert Downey Jr., started so similarly and so brilliantly as a critically wounded man trying to figure out how to survive in a cave halfway around the world before ultimately slogging through that horrible lava-people threequel by the time his solo run ended – but Spider-Man keeps delivering for me again and again. And I think I know why: it’s because, to quote Yelena, Brand New Day – and Holland’s solo Spider-Man films by and large – keep “small potatoes” stakes.

It’s inevitable that as sequels build on what’s come before – particularly one in which all of the films live in the same cinematic universe – the stakes get higher. But my favorite MCU films, with Spider-Man being the best example, have focused on the micro rather than the macro. Peter Parker’s problems have largely been his own: balancing schoolwork and superhero work, managing his feelings for his high-school crush, trying to protect the only family he has, and in Brand New Day, trying (and failing) to wield his great power responsibly all by himself.

My favorite MCU films, with Spider-Man being the best example, have focused on the micro rather than the macro.

More broadly, Brand New Day excels because it is clearly and unmistakably about Peter Parker and his struggles with being a superhero in New York City. Yes, the Hulk is in it, and Yelena Belova is in it, and Frank “The Punisher” Castle is in it a whole lot – but they aren’t there to solve galaxy-sized problems. Even the (apparent) villain in Brand New Day isn’t trying to end the world or take it over; instead, she’s just trying to find her sister.

Side note on Castle: I absolutely cherish Bernthal’s brilliant portrayal of that tortured character, and coming into Brand New Day and knowing it wasn’t rated R, I worried that we’d get a really lame, watered-down version of The Punisher. And while we certainly don’t see any One Last Kill-style rampages, Castle completely works in this movie because it focuses on his small-scale but nevertheless relatable problem that’s central to his character: his loneliness – his “sentence,” as he calls it – and how his burgeoning friendship with Spider-Man can help bring him out of his self-imposed darkness.

But back to Peter Parker and Spider-Man. The first Holland solo film, Homecoming, is a grounded, New York-specific story (minus the academic decathlon team’s trip to Washington, D.C.) about coming to terms with high-school life when you have newfound superpowers. Its follow-up, Far From Home, takes the gang to Europe, but still grounds the story around Peter, MJ, and Ned. The third film, No Way Home, tugged at my heartstrings more than any MCU movie since Endgame by bringing Andrew Garfield and Tobey Maguire back into the fold, but in the end, it’s still about Peter having to suffer the burden of his superhero life by saying goodbye to his best friend and the girl he loves – not to mention the only parental figure he has left in his life. And Brand New Day sees Peter struggle with bearing the weight of that burden alone before realizing that we all need people we can count on in order to get through this life, with or without arachnid DNA.

These sorts of local, intra-character problems are the most relatable, which is perhaps why all four Spider-Man films in the MCU have clicked so well with me while so many others – particularly recent ones – haven’t. After all, this is how the MCU started: with an egotistical man held prisoner in critical condition, put there by the weapons built by his own company. Tony Stark’s internal journey from apathetic billionaire playboy to someone who uses his power for good is what endeared us to him in the first place. And so too has it been for Tom Holland’s Spider-Man. I’d argue that Holland gives his best portrayal of Peter Parker yet in Brand New Day, and it’s because the story focuses on his individual journey rather than one with multiverse-moving stakes. You know, small potatoes. I hope Marvel, Sony, and Holland never lose sight of it.

https://www.ign.com/articles/battle-in-t.title: Battle in the Flower Gardens Is a Video Game-Infused Coming-of-Age Story
https://www.ign.com/articles/battle-in-t.content:
Having trained under no less a modern master than American Vampire co-creator Rafael Albuquerque, Brazilian cartoonist Eduardo Medeiros is definitely a rising star in the comic book world. Medeiros is following up projects like Roderick and the City of Morhil and Funny Creek with Battle in the Flower Gardens, a coming-of-age story with a heavy dose of video game-flavored nostalgia.

IGN can exclusively debut the first preview of this new Comixology Originals graphic novel. Check it out in the slideshow gallery below:

Batte in the Flower Gardens is written, drawn, and colored by Medeiros, with lettering by Deyvison Manes. Here's Comixology's official description of the book:

Set in a beautiful beachside town, Battle in the Flower Gardens follows two adolescents on the precipice of adulthood. Culling from real life experience, Medeiros weaves a story of joy, sadness, and the magical feeling of summers that last forever, that will keep the reader engaged until the very last page. As for the art, Medeiros has divided the look of the art into two distinct and compelling styles to capture the journey of self-discovery and growth the character is experiencing.
Every summer, Luke goes to the beach with his parents and his best friend, Mitchell, with whom he shares various geek interests and pastimes. But this summer everything changes, testing and altering their friendship forever.
Like many teenagers in the 90s, Luke and Mitchell find refuge from their parents and the real world in the arcades. As the summer lingers on, the boys struggle to navigate their friendship, culminating in a battle over video game skills that has real life consequences and will reverberate amongst the teenagers forever.

"Battle in the Flower Gardens is a story I’ve been wanting to tell for a long time," said Medeiros in a statement. "When I was a young boy, my family had a tradition of spending every summer at Capão Novo, a beachside town in southern Brazil. It's where I have some of my fondest memories and much of that has found its way into this book."

Medeiros continued, "This book is deeply personal and the process of creating it took me on a sweet journey back to the days of my youth. I hope readers enjoy the story and I encourage them to reminisce about the experiences that have shaped them."

Battle in the Flower Gardens will be released on the Comixology platform on August 25, 2026.

https://www.ign.com/articles/game-of-thr.title: Game of Thrones Author George R.R. Martin Shares Personal Update, Discusses Health and 'Falling Further and Further Behind'
https://www.ign.com/articles/game-of-thr.content:
77-year-old Game of Thrones author George R.R. Martin has shared a candid update on his health, and discussed "falling further and further behind."

Penning his first entry in six months on his personal blog, Martin acknowledged the lack of recent updates and described the year so far as having been "stressful, to say the least."

"So much has been happening, it's been overwhelming," Martin wrote in a post titled 'Better Late Than Never.' "Some great things, exciting things. Dreams coming true. But there have been nightmares too. I have lost friends. Battled sadness and depression. The worst may be yet to come.

"I turned 77 last September, and I tell you, getting old is no fun," Martin continued. "But there have been amazing times as well."

Ending the blog on a more positive note, Martin celebrated the nine Emmy nominations recently secured by Game of Thrones spinoff A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms and said he "will try and catch up some" on posting in future.

No mention was made in the post on what Martin has been working on recently, and there was (perhaps unsurprisingly) also no mention of House of the Dragon, after Martin previously described his working relationship with showrunner Ryan Condal as "abysmal."

Martin has previously discussed losing fellow authors and peers, as well as his friend, Hollywood legend Robert Redford, who came out of retirement last year for a brief cameo with Martin in his AMC series Dark Winds. Speaking earlier this year, Martin also said that if he never completes Game of Thrones sequel Winds of Winter (or the book after that), there's no plan for anyone else to step in. Instead, his Song of Ice and Fire series simply "won't be finished."

Speaking to The Hollywood Reporter about his lack of progress on his next novel, Martin said he would "hate" to give up on the series — though admitted he had made little progress in recent years. At the same time, Martin has served as a producer on Game of Thrones' various TV spinoffs and Dark Winds, and continued publishing of various A Song of Ice and Fire companion novels — with at least two new Dunk and Egg adventures also currently left part-finished.

The Game of Thrones franchise shows no sign of slowing down, however, with a new stage play set to begin soon in the U.K., and early plans for a potential HBO Game of Thrones sequel series starring Arya Stark.

https://www.ign.com/articles/spider-man-.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Hides a Secret Character Who's Already Appeared in a String of MCU Movies and Could Become the Next Spider Superhero
https://www.ign.com/articles/spider-man-.content:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day hides an appearance by yet another Marvel Comics superhero — someone who has quietly made cameos in previous Spider-Man and Avengers movies. Did you spot them?

In the comics, Cindy Moon is well known via her alter ego Silk, who begins her superhero journey as a Korean-American student bitten by the same spider as Peter Parker. But fewer fans will know that Cindy has also been quietly teased within the MCU for a decade, with appearances in a string of films.

In Brand New Day, Cindy is the student in Bruce Banner's class who asks the question about Thanos — why the big purple baddie didn't just double the universe's resources instead of killing half of its life. It's a blink-and-you'll-miss-it moment (and a good question!), but actually the latest in a consistent series of cameos.

Why isn’t anyone talking about this!?!

Cindy Moon was in Dr.Banner’s Class#SpiderManBrandNewDay pic.twitter.com/NBg1eitRxU

— •tr1stan⛷️ (@nuel_irl) July 31, 2026

Cindy first appeared in Spider-Man: Homecoming, portrayed by actress Tiffany Espensen, and makes numerous appearances throughout the movie as one of Peter's classmates. While Cindy largely remains in the background, she still has a few lines of dialogue — enough that her character remains notable enough to appear again in future.

Audiences next glimpsed Cindy in Avengers: Infinity War, on the same school bus as Peter and Ned, again played by Espensen. Fast forward to Spider-Man: No Way Home, and Cindy returns one more time via the film's extended cut post-credit scene that features previously-unused footage.

I’m literally dropping a video later today on this.

They are different actress and the build up story is all over the place for Cindy moon.

And the cancellation of the silk spider society show would have played into the SSU spiderverse Sony is building 🤙 https://t.co/v2WC731d06

— KING SPYKE (@KingSpyke_) August 3, 2026

With Espensen now seemingly retired from acting, Brand New Day sees Shannon Young Cho take on Cindy's role — and continue on the character in Tom Holland's second trilogy of films. But where is this all going? Is Marvel playing the long game with Cindy's introduction, or is this just a fun set of Easter eggs for Cindy Moon fans?

"Seeing the same character in three movies doesn't feel random," one fan wrote wrote on social media. "It looks like Marvel is slowly setting up something bigger."

"Marvel/Sony are definitely slowly soft launching Cindy Moon to the general public more and more and I cannot wait to see Silk," said another.

"Cindy f***ing Moon has more MCU appearances than Shang Chi," noted another fan.

While Cindy's MCU future isn't yet certain, the jaw-dropping success of Brand New Day now makes Spider-Man 5 seem inevitable. Perhaps we'll finally see Silk emerge then?

https://www.ign.com/articles/she-ended-o.title: 'She Ended on a Really Great Note': Jessica Henwick Says She's Turned Down Returning as Colleen Wing in Daredevil: Born Again Season 3
https://www.ign.com/articles/she-ended-o.content:
Iron Fist star Jessica Henwick has said her character Colleen Wing won't return in Daredevil: Born Again Season 3, despite talks with Marvel.

Wing previously appeared in the Netflix series Iron Fist, Luke Cage and The Defenders, and eventually inherited the Iron Fist mantle from the show's lead character, Danny Rand.

Fans had hoped that Colleen Wing would make her return in the upcoming third season of Daredevil: Born Again, which is expected to reunite the main four Defenders for the first time in almost a decade. However, Henwick has said that while she had discussed returning in the role with Marvel, she ultimately opted to pass on the opportunity.

"I've said multiple times over the years, I would love to come back. I know that everyone is back this season. I'm not in this season," Henwick told Inverse. "We did have discussions about whether I should go back this season. But for me, her story ended with her going off into the sunset. She has the Iron Fist. She's got Misty by her side. Daughters of the Dragon is happening. She ended on a really great note."

Any future storyline involving Colleen needed to be worth "unpicking" that ending, Henwick continued, rather than having her return only to be "just stood in the back of the shot."

"I'm just not interested in bringing her back unless it's worth sort of unpicking that happiness, because obviously she can't be happy on a TV series," Henwick concluded. "If she's back, something's gone wrong. I would absolutely love to come back, but it would just really have to be the right story."

Famously, Henwick previously turned down an appearance as a different character in Marvel movie Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings, in the hope that Colleen Wing could still return in future. (This was before Daredevil: Born Again came along and began reviving Marvel's Netflix era in full force.)

It sounds like Henwick is still keen to make a return as Colleen Wing someday, then, but don't expect to see her when Daredevil: Born Again Season 3 debuts in spring 2027. The only question now, however, is whether Daredevil: Born Again will continue on and get a Season 4.

The past week has seen Marvel scrap its planned Season 2 of Emmy-nominated series Wonder Man, leaving the brand's live-action TV future in doubt. Currently, just Daredevil: Born Again and Vision Quest are on Marvel's upcoming TV slate, and both have already finished filming. No further series or seasons are yet believed to be greenlit.

https://www.ign.com/articles/spider-man-.title: Spider-Man: No Way Home's Mary Rivera, Ned's Grandma, Has Died Aged 82
https://www.ign.com/articles/spider-man-.content:
Mary Rivera, the actress who played Ned's Grandma in Spider-Man: No Way Home, has died aged 82.

While Rivera's contribution to Spider-Man: No Way Home was relatively short, her scene-stealing performance made her an instantly memorable addition to the movie's cast. And, even more impressively, this was despite the fact that the 2021 blockbuster was Rivera's only acting role.

Rivera's family previously revealed how they encouraged Mary to audition for the part after spotting a casting call advert posted to Facebook.

"I happened to be on a friend's Facebook scrolling," Rivera's daughter Kelly told Hawai'i Public Radio, "and I see an ad, a casting call looking for a local Hawai'i Filipina grandmother between the age of 50 and 90. And immediately I thought, 'Oh, well my mom qualifies and checks off all those boxes.'

"They just asked her to talk about herself and why she wanted to do the role. So she just gave a brief history of her time in the Philippines and what brought her to the United States, and raising her four children and 11 grandchildren — and basically that that is her biggest accomplishment of everything that she's done," Kelly added. "My mom has worn many hats over the years. She was a radio broadcaster, a teacher, but most notable was her role as a mother and grandmother."

Sadly, Rivera suffered a serious stroke in April and never recovered, TMZ has reported.

Jacob Batalon, who plays Ned in the Spider-Man franchise, has since offered his own message of condolence via Instagram, writing: "REST IN PARADISE LOLA😭❤️❤️❤️."

Five years on, Ned has returned in the just-released Spider-Man: Brand New Day, which has already notched up nearly $1 billion at the box office. Perhaps the inevitable sequel will include a tribute to Rivera?
