https://www.ign.com/articles/ice-cream-m.title: Ice Cream Man Review
https://www.ign.com/articles/ice-cream-m.content:
Ice Cream Man will be released in theaters on August 7.

Eli Roth is no stranger to violence. Over the course of his career, from directing unrelentingly gruesome films like Hostel and the darkly fun yet forgettable recent Thanksgiving to playing a brief yet memorable part in Inglorious Basterds, he’s made blood and viscera the materials with which he paints. Sometimes, this has yielded results you can’t help but be begrudgingly captivated by, where the more the blood runs, the more you can’t bring yourself to look away. Still, in many other cases (looking at you, Cabin Fever and The Green Inferno), it’s felt like Roth was shamelessly lifting ideas from older, far better movies without adding anything new. Rather than feeling like homage, they’re closer to poor imitation. Instead of being remotely horrifying, the scariest thing about a growing number of Roth’s films — when they aren’t outright disasters like the baffling Borderlands — is how derivative they are.

Such is the case with Ice Cream Man, Roth’s first film directed under his company, The Horror Section. Not to be confused with the 1995 horror movie of the same name starring Clint Howard, this is a film about the dangers of consuming too much ice cream that itself feels like it’s gobbled up too many past horror films and puked them out. However, what’s strange this time around is how his latest is not just indebted to horror of the distant past, but recent genre hits like the Terrifier series and Zach Cregger’s Weapons. It’s once more not nearly as good as either of those, lacking the chaotic madness of Art the Clown in its killer and the more haunting yet humorous patience with which Cregger approached his stellar horror film. Instead, it’s just a sporadic smashing together of both of them, bringing together murderous kids trapped in a trance of some kind, and a silent though far less entertainingly expressive killer pulling their strings. The primary difference? The reason for the kids becoming murderous involves eating ice cream.

Credit where credit is due: This is not the worst premise on paper, and even sounds like it could be the start of a more campy, cheeky horror romp. Unfortunately, Roth never makes the most of this potential, resulting in a film that’s really cheap and less than clever. This cheapness extends both to the way it all looks as well as the way it’s constructed. From the opening moments surrounding a baseball game that will soon be the last any in this town ever play, it feels like you’re watching a YouTube sketch rather than an immersive horror film. There isn’t any richness or texture to the images, most of the scenes are bizarrely overlit, and lines of dialogue feel painfully cringeworthy in a way that only seems half intentional. The more that it goes on, the more the whole thing proves inescapably awkward and stiff rather than playfully unhinged. Even when a character later gets their cranium removed so that their brain can be scooped out and fed back to them, it elicits little more than a shrug. It’s a movie that inflicts plenty of head trauma but ultimately reveals itself as having no real brains of its own.

At the core of it all is young Jared (Charlie Zeltzer), who — despite being lactose intolerant — will still be tormented by the titular Ice Cream Man (Ari Millen) after he unleashes what is essentially a curse on the otherwise peaceful Bayleen Bay. There’s a vaguely Stephen King-esque feel to the town, but we quickly realize how limited in scope it all is. Rather than feel like a real place populated by memorable characters or with interesting environments for the horror to play out in, it’s all rather unimaginative and just about getting to the next burst of violence, which often does prove genuinely gruesome. Parents are murdered in their beds by their children, the school becomes a site of bloody violence, and the town is revealed as having a darker side that the community has (futilely) tried to keep hidden. Some of this is sufficiently preposterous, with kills involving microscopes, a ladder, and even a Segway all bringing plenty of blood to the table.

That’s where the film seems to be attempting to be more like Terrifier, but where that movie — for all its flaws and own budgetary limitations — boasted great performances in lead Lauren LaVera and David Howard Thornton as Art himself, as well as a real sense of go-for-broke mania, there’s nothing here that brings the necessary energy to make this ride come alive. Instead, we get Roth himself playing Jared’s father and delivering lines like, “Dare I say, he gives me the chills,” in reference to the Ice Cream Man, which repeatedly fall flat. Were the film more playful throughout, maybe moments like this could work; instead, this line lands awkwardly and is followed by one of the most truly strange dubbed lines you’ll ever hear when Roth’s character turns away. It’s all more amateurish than it is darkly absurd, giving you a “we have Terrifier at home” feeling.

The Ice Cream Man is no Art the Clown or Aunt Gladys, and Roth is no horror auteur.

Most disappointingly, when it comes to what this horror film attempts to serve up, there just isn’t that much to chew on. It’s never quite creatively ridiculous enough to go off the rails, and the scenes where we’re spoon-fed mounds of rather unnecessary exposition grind everything to a halt. Where the grim pleasures to be found in Weapons were balanced by a creeping sense of dread, Roth’s Ice Cream Man doesn’t earn either. It occasionally gestures towards playing around with some animated sequences, only for those to fall by the wayside. For all it throws at the wall to see what sticks, the surface stays pretty bare. Despite running less than 90 minutes, you will feel the length; a sudden swerve to dive into the backstory of its killer just results in a dreary drawn-out explanation.

In the end, despite how desperately it attempts to replicate what’s been done better elsewhere, the Ice Cream Man is no Art the Clown or Aunt Gladys, and Roth is no horror auteur. Where Weapons was restrained before ending with a bang, providing a dark cherry on top with one of the most satisfying yet sinister endings of recent memory, this film fails to build in any entertaining way and just leaves you with a sense of emptiness. The only real revelation that you come away with is that you could probably entirely skip this meal, including the dessert that is supposedly so important, and not miss much. You won’t be screaming in either joy or fear, but you will open your mouth to yawn.

https://www.ign.com/articles/beast-of-re.title: Beast of Reincarnation Review
https://www.ign.com/articles/beast-of-re.content:
Like an above-ground swimming pool, Beast of Reincarnation is one of those things that feels like it should be great in theory, but leaves something to be desired once you actually spend some time in it. On a surface level, everything from the aesthetics and otherworldly apocalyptic setting to the battles against giant, diseased creatures has the makings of something really special. In practice though, this awesome collection of ideas only rarely approaches realizing that potential, as nearly every aspect proves to be quite shallow. Combat against both minion enemies and bosses alike is extremely one-note, the story succeeds much more at collecting tropes than evoking any kind of emotion, and there’s an overreliance on indistinguishable areas and enemies throughout the adventure. There’s still a decent action RPG in here somewhere, because when it occasionally does shine with a neat wrinkle in the story or a particularly cool fight sequence, it’s very easy to see how this could have been every bit as awesome as it looks at first glance, but highlights like those are certainly the exception to an action game that’s largely just okay.

Combining elements of a soulslike with a more traditional JRPG, this fast-paced action game feels like what you might end up with if you tried to combine Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice with the Final Fantasy VII Remake. Across the roughly 35-hour campaign, you’ll split your time between exploring levels of ruined buildings reclaimed by wildlife, parrying and dodging in tense combat encounters, and learning about the convoluted backstory of the world and characters that surround your protagonist, Emma. There’s loads of potential in that formula, and in its best moments, Beast of Reincarnation is both beautiful to look at and incredibly badass, as your katana-wielding elemental mage absolutely overloads the screen with over-the-top melee attacks, sending bolts of lightning and fire flying every which way to complement the artful swordsmanship.

That potential is only realized every once in a while though, as you’ll spend a lot of your time fighting the same handful of enemies far too often, plowing through even the most daunting encounters without much friction due to incredibly forgiving parry windows, and quickly mastering every opponent you come across owing to the fact that they all have just two or three attacks they repeat ad nauseum. Conceptually, ninja-dueling your way through this beautiful, destroyed world and its massive monsters should be sick as hell, but it only takes a couple hours for it all to feel quite skin deep, like how in its opening chapter you’re forced to fight the same giant elk boss multiple times, as it assails you with the one attack it seem to know over and over again in a fight that lasts much longer than it should.

There are still plenty of memorable moments sprout up every now and then, like one level where you’re scaling the inside of a creepy, rotating cube machine and fighting against the forgotten experiments left in the creepy structure, but most of your time will be spent in forgettable regions filled with the same robotic baddies, concluding in a boss fight against a creature you’ve already seen (and is in many cases just a larger version of an existing bestial enemy).

One aspect of combat that fares much better is the addition of Koo, your dire wolf companion, who battles alongside you with an arsenal of increasingly destructive magical abilities. Koo mostly does his own thing, but his behaviors and abilities can be customized and upgraded as you go, and it's important to build him up accordingly since he becomes a vital part of getting through some of the larger combat sequences much faster. He can also be controlled directly, as you pause time to select a special ability for him to use Final Fantasy VII Remake-style – you can even command him to assassinate enemies on your behalf, which really helps speed up some of those repetitive combat encounters and can burn through large chunks of a boss’ health bar as well. Plus, Koo is inexplicably one of the strongest characters, despite being a four-legged pooch with no dialogue. His high energy and unusually expressive face serves as a counterweight to the robotic mannerisms of the majority of the bipedal cast.

The paper-thin depth of Beast of Reincarnation only grows the longer you play.

Despite Koo’s best efforts though, the paper-thin depth of Beast of Reincarnation only grows the longer you play. Exploring the mostly-linear regions is beautiful and features some truly awesome music, but after just two levels I already felt overly familiar with the extremely monotonous checklist of loot to collect and camp sites to unlock before fighting the boss (almost always twice for some reason), then moving on to do it all again. That formula doesn’t evolve as you progress through levels either, as you only ever unlock new abilities to help you power through combat while exploration and platforming never gain any new tricks. Meanwhile, most of the combat pits you against sword-wielding automatons who have maybe one or two different attacks between them, which means you’ll be parrying and countering the same set of telegraphed attacks a dozen times in a single combat encounter.

Even things like the music (which again, is quite good), becomes stale as you quickly discover they’ve got one whole song playing on a loop for more than ten hours worth of levels. Emma, on the other hand, gains access to a bunch of passive abilities that buff her generally, and a bunch of special arts that unlock new moves and attack combos in combat. Most of this stuff does very little to make fighting feel better, as you’re still going up against enemies that just spam the same attacks for you to parry before countering with an attack of your own. They do help those fights go by much quicker, however, and eventually you’ll be able to take out a handful of enemies all at once with some seriously cool-looking attacks.

RPG mechanics don’t fare much better, as the shallow upgrades available for upgrading your katanas, ranged weapons, and accessories are fairly limited. For example, you’ll find new katanas on a regular basis, but even by the end of the story, you won’t come across any that are definitively better or have incentives to support a specific playstyle than those you found early on. So, you have little motivation to upgrade them except to diversify the special effects and status ailments various weapons offer. Skill trees, on the other hand, fare much better as Koo unlocks a whole host of abilities that blast enemies with tons of high-DPS spells and layer on status effects that do things like bind an enemy in place with magical plant vines.

Boss fights are especially disappointing, because they feel like they should be the major draw here, but instead only serve to magnify combat’s shortcomings (quite literally) as you fight a massive beast whose imposing presence is wasted on them being incredibly thoughtless adversaries who often repeat the same slow-moving attack twenty times in row. Bizarrely, you’re usually made to fight these creatures once partway through a level, only to face them again with zero changes at the level’s conclusion, before they transform into an even cooler-looking final phase that…attacks with an almost identical moveset. Worse yet, in the second half of the adventure, it seems to straight up run out of ideas as it starts sending repeat bosses at you. The fact that all of these fights are followed by the same cutscene of your character passing out then waking up in a bed certainly don’t help, making story progress fall into a predictable cadence.

Like any RPG worth its salt, a lot of the focus here is on the story, complete with cutscenes so lengthy you’ll want to remember to flick the joystick every so often to keep your screen lit up. As an emotionless warrior who also has amnesia (because of course you do), you’ll go around hunting down the aforementioned giant, blighted beasts alongside Koo, so you can stop the end of the world. As is the case with lots of things in Beast of Reincarnation, that idea is much stronger than the execution as Emma and the apocalyptic setting that gives rise to such conflict is poised to deliver a tale filled with interesting mysteries to unravel. Instead, Emma and her companions come with lifeless performances as they tell a story with every single genre trope in the book, including a quiet hero who has been chosen by prophecy, a heavy-handed nature vs. humans/technology theme, a Force-ghost little girl who isn’t actually there, and an amnesiatic character who at one point is stricken with a second dose of amnesia so she remembers even less than before.

None of that would be a deal-breaker for me were it not for the fact that the execution of its trope-filled story isn't delivered with the kind of punch that can make up for it. It's on the weaker side with consistently weak dialogue and reveals I saw coming from about 10 miles away. If you’ve played a JRPG in the last twenty years, there’s nothing about this story that hasn’t been done better in numerous other games, and if you’re expecting the quality to be near the level of something like Xenoblade Chronicles, you’re almost certainly going to be disappointed. It’s especially weird just how flat most of the characters are; they rarely show emotion (sometimes with in-universe reasons, not that the justification makes it more interesting to watch). The robotic animations, lifeless eyes, and long silences in between dialogue makes nearly all the scenes between Emma and her found family pretty hard to sit through most of the time. And they do that thing where they show a washed out flashback to something that literally happened less than five minutes ago, which drives me up the wall way more than it probably should.

Its trope-filled story isn't delivered with the kind of punch that can make up for it.

Also, this isn't really a specific pain point, but I feel obligated to mention just how much of the dialogue is taken up by characters talking about food and the eating of it. It'd make sense if it was woven in thematically, but it's not and I’m not sure if the writers were just super hungry when they wrote this or what, but it’s pretty bizarre.

The DJI Neo 4K is an excellent quadcopter drone camera for beginners looking to try out aerial videography. It doesn't require FAA registration, it automates most essential functions, it has built-in image stabilization, and thanks to today's deal, it's even more affordable. For a limited time, you can pick up the drone for just $139 or one of the Fly More combos for a little bit extra. Note that, according to PCMag, although the FCC has already banned new and upcoming foreign-made drones from being sold in the United States, existing drone models can still be purchased legally.

Save 30% Off the DJI Neo 4K Drone Camera

The DJI Neo 4K is a petite drone that weighs in at a miniscule 135 grams, or just under 5 ounces. That means this quadcopter doesn't have to be registered with the FAA. It's so light that even if you use the heavier extended battery, you're still under the 249 gram cutoff. If you do want to register anyway, it's only $5 and remains valid for 3 years.

The Neo measures 5" x 6" x 2" and packs away easily because of its compact size. It's designed to be used outdoors and is rated to withstand up to Level 4 winds (13-18mph), although it's good practice to take it out in slightly less powerful winds as a safety buffer. Brushless motors allow the Mini 4K to travel at a zippy horizontal top speed of up to 35mph.

If you buy the Neo by itself, you'll control it using your smartphone app. The range is restricted to 30m (150 feet). If you get either of the Fly More Combos, you'll get a remote that boosts the horizontal range up to 10,000km (4,000m vertical) under ideal conditions. Real world range is much lower because you really want to maintain line of sight at all times since the remote uses OcuSync technology. The stock battery will give you up to 18 minutes of runtime.

Because this is a camera designed for beginners, it has intelligent features to assist you in piloting the drone properly. Automated functions include one-tap takeoff and landing, GPS Return to Base (RTB), and stable hovering. The rotors have integrated propeller guards so you don't have to worry about chipped blades every time you screw up a landing. The built-in 4K camera records directly onto the 22GB onboard storage (there's no option to expand the capacity with memory cards) and has built-in electronic image stabilization instead of a gimbal like the higher-end models. Framing and composing your shot is straightforward with an array of preset video techniques like Helix, Dronie, Rocket, and Boomerang.

There are three bundles you can choose from. For $199 you can get three additional batteries and the charger. This is an outstanding value because it's only $60 more than the drone itself and OEM batteries are not cheap. For $245, the Fly More combo gets you two extra batteries and the DJI RC-N3 remote. Finally, for $369, the Motion Fly More combo swaps out the remote with the DJI goggles and RC Motion 3 controller for a super immersive control experience.

https://www.ign.com/articles/x-men-fans-.title: X-Men Fans Are Rediscovering That Samara Weaving Is a Huge Gamer After Emma Frost Casting
https://www.ign.com/articles/x-men-fans-.content:
X-Men fans were more hyped than ever after Samara Weaving was cast as Emma Frost, but they got even more geeked after discovering that she’s a very serious gamer.

Samara Weaving is your new Emma Frost. Beyond her astonishing resemblance to the glamorous mutant (that face card could not be more perfect for Emma), she’s also a loveable goofball and a massive gamer, something that came back to light once news of her casting hit the internet.

Back in March, Weaving spoke with IGN alongside fellow Ready or Not 2 star Kathryn Newton about their shared love for video games, revealing a wide variety of favorites that included Assassin’s Creed, Red Dead Redemption 2, Hogwarts Legacy, and even Mortal Kombat.

“I like an open world,” she told us, going on to say that her Mortal Kombat main is Kitana.

“I’m really good at it,” she said of the fighting game series. (Speaking of which, her friend, Jessica McNamee, plays Sonya Blade in the recent movies).

And in June 2026, Weaving gushed about her gaming habits in an episode of Polygon’s Shelf Quest, revealing that she hauls her PS5 with her everywhere she goes.

“All my jobs, I pack my PlayStation 5 in my suitcase, which is insane. It takes up half the suitcase and no one can lift it and they all hate me. But I bring it to every AirBnB and hotel that I stay at,” she told the outlet while standing among the crowded shelves of Videogamesnewyork.

In the interview, she revealed that her parents didn’t allow her to play video games growing up, saying she often played at friends’ houses when she could. She also reiterated her love of open world games, citing all the exploration and free-range roaming they allow.

But when it comes to fighting games, Weaving says they just ‘speak’ to her, saying she finds great success quite easily in both Mortal Kombat and Street Fighter.

“[Mortal Kombat] and Street Fighter, surprisingly, [I] was really good, really quick. I can beat a lot of people at Mortal Kombat. I don’t know why. It speaks to me, especially the chick with the fans — Kitana — I’m really good at Kitana. She’s my gal. She’s my fave.”

These interviews have sprung back up into the public consciousness, prompting no end of excitement and jokes as fans wait anxiously for more news on the X-Men reboot film.

“Imagine you’re getting your ass kicked by a Kitana, and it's her,” one wrote on X.

“She's rapidly climbing up the ladder of my fav actresses!” another said.

“Maybe she plays Marvel Rivals and plays Emma Frost,” yet another speculated.

While we can’t know that for certain just yet, we do have a few more details about the upcoming X-Men reboot film, directed by Jake Schreier. A number of other roles are currently undergoing casting, which reportedly began back in May, leaving fans even more hopeful for spot-on casting news in the near future.

With D23 set for August 14-16, there’s a good chance Marvel will reveal what it’s got up its sleeves, especially since it was so tight-lipped during its Hall H panel at San Diego Comic-Con in July.

Image Credits: Michael Tullberg/Getty Images / NetEase Games, Marvel Games

https://www.ign.com/articles/shift-up-ce.title: Shift Up CEO Defends Stellar Blade: Blood Rain AI Music Video Against Player Backlash
https://www.ign.com/articles/shift-up-ce.content:
The CEO of Shift Up has responded to backlash surrounding the release of an AI-generated music video promoting Stellar Blade’s sequel game, Blood Rain.

The video, published on July 31, showed the game’s main character, Evie, singing and dancing to an upbeat pop song titled "Wanna be in Love." It’s very obviously AI-generated, containing all the signature tells of such content, including nonsensical written wording, inconsistencies in character models, and a blurred, airbrushed filter over it all.

This has soured players on the otherwise highly-anticipated title, prompting a harsh wave of criticism that warranted a response from developer Shift Up’s CEO, Kim Hyung Tae.

"Wanna be in LOVE" feat. EVIE from Stellar Blade : BLOODRAIN
EVIE’s new music video is now available in YouTube. I would be very grateful if you could watch the video and share your thoughts! https://t.co/n1bhFiH1IJ#StellarBlade #BLOODRAIN #EVIE pic.twitter.com/eNiLyZAQ5W

— Kim Hyung Tae, 김형태, キム・ヒョンテ (@jamm3rd) July 31, 2026

Speaking on X (formerly Twitter), Kim praised the artists responsible for the design of the game’s main character, Evie, arguing that an AI merely used their work to compile the scenes showing her dancing and singing rather than making anything on its own from scratch.

“EVIE, the character at the heart of this video, was created from head to toe by our talented artists and modelers through more than a year of dedicated work. The AI is not creating her from scratch. It is rendering and presenting the character based on the data, designs, and craftsmanship our team created. We would truly appreciate it if you could view the work with that understanding in mind,” he wrote.

Unsurprisingly, this explanation didn’t put players’ minds at ease. If anything, it left them even more frustrated and somewhat confused, with some pointing out that training an AI model on the designs of Shift Up’s designers does them a disservice and even bastardizes the artistry behind all their hard work.

EVIE, the character at the heart of this video, was created from head to toe by our talented artists and modelers through more than a year of dedicated work.

The AI is not creating her from scratch. It is rendering and presenting the character based on the data, designs, and…

— Kim Hyung Tae, 김형태, キム・ヒョンテ (@jamm3rd) July 31, 2026

“The AI is doing your character a disservice, distorting her appearance, and in turn, making your team's art look bad, when in reality, they're so talented,” one fan wrote on X. “I would rather have fewer, shorter cinematics of your characters made by animators than hours of uncanny AI generations.”

“That’s the issue though, it does not look like her a lot of the time, even if they might use the base model as part of the input. You're diminishing the quality of your own work, the brand, the studio, and Evie as a character,” another argued.

“You also risk associating the brand with AI slop, even if that might be true or not. You risk being in a position where the game might have some amazing set pieces or city backdrops that designers and developers made, and people will dismiss it as AI-generated.”

It’s worth noting that this is merely a music video promoting Stellar Blade: Blood Rain and not the game itself. However, Kim has previously remarked on AI in reference to Korea’s competition with China in the gaming space, claiming Shift Up doesn’t have the manpower to compete with Chinese studios.

"80% of our company's revenue comes from overseas, and when we go abroad, the first opponent we encounter is Chinese games. We pour about 150 people into a single game, but China invests 1,000 to 2,000. We lack the capability to compete in terms of the quality or quantity of content,” he said back in January, per GameMeca.

"I do not think people will lose their jobs even if AI becomes widespread. Even if we mobilize all available manpower, it will not be enough, and I believe that we can only barely compete with industries like China or the United States that require massive workforce deployments if all these people are proficient in AI and one person can perform the role of 100."

What’s more, Kim predicted a future where AI is central to the games industry, pointing out how quickly young people are picking it up as an essential tool in daily life.

"(Korea's) ChatGPT paid subscription rate ranks second after the United States. The new generation is natural to AI. I believe that AI is the future of the younger generation and can become a new vision applicable to industry."

The Stellar Blade games themselves are no stranger to controversy, with Kim most recently addressing the debate that cropped up around Evie’s youthful design following Blood Rain’s reveal at Summer Game Fest. Given how sexualized Eve was in Stellar Blade, players were worried about how Evie might be perceived by some fans.

Speaking with IGN, the Shift Up CEO promised that “if you actually play the game, you will not think that,” telling us that, when combined with her scrappy nature and other features, players will “see that she’s a very lovable character.”

https://www.ign.com/articles/rockstar-ga.title: Rockstar Games Killed Midnight Club 5 Because It Wasn't as Big as GTA, Ex-Designer Claims
https://www.ign.com/articles/rockstar-ga.content:
An ex-Rockstar Games designer claims that the studio killed the Midnight Club franchise as it wasn't as big as Grand Theft Auto.

In an interview with Insider Gaming, former Rockstar senior designer Kris Roberts was asked about Midnight Club's fate, having worked on the franchise at Rockstar San Diego — the studio that helmed Rockstar's arcade racing franchise and led development on the first Red Dead Redemption. Roberts noted that a fifth Midnight Club game was in early development following the release of Midnight Club: Los Angeles and the team had even prototyped new locations, including London.

Unfortunately, the plug was pulled on the racing game during its development phase. Roberts noted that there was a "non-trivial conflict" between Rockstar San Diego and the more central Rockstar New York. The designer noted that while there had been legitimate frustrations over missed deadlines on the previous Midnight Club game, Rockstar still hadn't given the racing series its props as it wasn't nearly as big as GTA.

“The perception was we never got the accolades or the reception,” Roberts explained. “The New York perspective was, ‘You’re not GTA’. When you’re the red-headed stepchild project — you know, we’re doing a good job, we’re world-class, but we’re still treated less than. It was challenging.”

Roberts also stated that Midnight Club kept players more engaged than competitors like Need for Speed and Burnout, but it wasn't enough. Unfortunately, the cancelation of Midnight Club 5 signaled to a lot of people that the franchise was unlikely to return and as a result, remaining staff moved on to work on Red Dead Redemption or other projects within Rockstar.

“When they cancelled it, it was pretty clear that there would be no more Midnight Club and everything was going to be GTA and stuff moving forward, and that’s just the way it was going to be," said Roberts.

One of the big complaints from fans is that Rockstar hasn't diversified enough since Grand Theft Auto 5. A sequel to Red Dead Redemption made sense as the studio's follow up, but it has now meant that Rockstar has been in a loop of GTA and Red Dead games for a decade and a half. Some fans fear this is the future of Rockstar and that we won't get more unique, smaller-scale games like Bully, LA Noire, or Midnight Club anymore.

Rockstar will have the opportunity to do whatever it wants after GTA 6, given it will make unfathomable amounts of money. The studio is publishing a pair of Max Payne remakes, developed by Remedy, but it's unclear when these will see the light of day. Whether or not Rockstar will revisit any of these dormant franchises itself or try something new after GTA 6 remains to be seen.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

https://www.ign.com/articles/pokemon-go-.title: Pokémon Go's LEGO Store Promotion is Now Live — Here's Where to Find a Location Near You
https://www.ign.com/articles/pokemon-go-.content:
Pokémon Go's LEGO collaboration is now live, bringing exclusive in-game rewards if you stop by a participating store — so, here's where to find one.

LEGO and Pokémon Go have teamed up this year as the former rolls out a range of Pokémon LEGO sets, many of which are infused with Smart Play technology. Pokémon Go also celebrated the European leg of its big summer events in Copenhagen, just a stone's throw from LEGO's global headquarters, and rolled out exclusive in-game bonuses.

Well, those in-game bonuses have thankfully become a lot easier to obtain for other Pokémon Go players, as long as you live in the U.S., Europe or Australia. Select LEGO stores across these regions now host all-day raids and sponsored PokéStops, which all bestow special goodies.

So, what do you get? Well, every day, each location will host one all-day raid that awards a Pikachu with a LEGO special background. Spinning the sponsored stops, meanwhile, will award LEGO Pokémon in-game stickers. Of course, you don't physically need to go into a LEGO store to get these bonuses, as you can interact with the in-game locations just by standing near. Indeed, head close enough and you'll also unlock an in-game Stamp Rally, which awards another Pikachu and records your progress if you visit further LEGO store locations.

With just over 200 participating stores, there's too many to list out here in full. However, an interactive map right here will now show you where to find the location closest to you.

In the U.S., the majority of states have at least one participating LEGO store. Over in Europe, the UK has around 20 — including four in London. And in mainland Europe, France, Germany and Poland also have local stores — though, strangely, there are none in Denmark.

This summer, Pokémon Go is celebrating its 10th year of operation (yes, it really has been a decade since it all began). Up next for the game will be its big end of summer Go Fest Finale event, where players expect more Mega Pokémon to make their debut, alongside other surprises. LEGO, meanwhile, has a fresh wave of Pokémon sets coming on October 1, including the $299.99 Iconic Trainer Moments: Poké Ball set, which will contain the first LEGO Pokémon minifigures.

https://www.ign.com/articles/rust-fan-su.title: Rust Fan Sues Police After Swatting Incident Leaves Him Paralyzed
https://www.ign.com/articles/rust-fan-su.content:
A Rust player left paralyzed by cops in a swatting incident is now suing the police for $176 million.

Back in April of this year, 23-year-old Tucson resident Axeel Melendez was shot in his leg and spine by two officers who stormed into his house via his bedroom window. The cops were responding to a false report of an active shooter in the building — despite Melendez previously warning their unit that he was being targeted by a potential swatter.

Melendez will likely remain paralyzed from the waist down for the rest of his life, and is now seeking damages for his medical expenses and wage losses.

Just two days before, Melendez had been hacked by another player of the survival game Rust, who accessed personal details on his computer and then demanded money not to release them publicly. Melendez didn't pay, and was then threatened with swatting — a practice where armed law enforcement is called to an address under false pretences.

Concerned for his safety, Melendez called 911 to report the threats and alert cops that his address could be swatted.

"They said that they were going to call the police station and say that I have a bomb so that FBI shows up at my house so I could get swatted," Melendez told a 911 responder, in a tape of the call reported by the Arizona Daily Star. "They knew my ethnicity, so they said that they were going to call ICE to show up at my house and get my whole family deported. We're all citizens, so it's okay."

In response, Melendez was told that a hoax caller "can't just call the SWAT on you" and that "nothing is going to happen."

An officer even visited Melendez's house to offer further reassurance, and state that deputies had been informed to be aware of fake emergency calls regarding his address. Regardless, just two days later, cops responded to a report that Melendez's father had shot his sister, and stormed the house with guns drawn.

Police video of the incident released into the public domain shows officers shouting from outside the house that they are from the sheriff's department, before giving up and using a shovel to smash Melendez's bedroom window. Seeing the end of Melendez's shotgun being pointed in their direction from behind a door, the officers open fire.

Melendez has said he was wearing noise-cancelling headphones to play games when the cops were outside, and only realized that someone was entering the house when his window was smashed. He then ran to wake his sleeping mother, and grabbed the family's legally-owned gun.

"My goal was to get some experience working on highline cars and then more advanced education in automotive engineering," Melendez said, reflecting on his life before he was paralyzed. "I really wanted to work on an F1 engineering team. I love soccer, and I enjoy reading and board games. I liked to be active and do stuff outside."

Local police have declined to comment on the matter further.

Swatting has sadly become a relatively common practice, and numerous video game fans who play or stream online have fallen victim. Grand Theft Auto 5 actor Ned Luke has been targeted numerous times, and recently celebrated one swatter finally receiving jail time.

https://www.ign.com/articles/marvels-wol.title: Marvel's Wolverine ESRB Rating Promises 'a Handful of Sequences' Featuring 'Exposed Buttocks'
https://www.ign.com/articles/marvels-wol.content:
Marvel's Wolverine will have gore, intense violence, strong language, and at least a few scenes featuring "a character's exposed buttocks," according to its Entertainment Software Rating Board (ESRB) rating.

The full description for Insomniac Games' M-rated superhero experience warned would-be players that "partial nudity" is one of the many elements they'll need to consider before picking up a copy this September (via MP1st). However, a more specific explanation toward the end of the page suggested the only example of this in the game might be one or two instances of on-screen butts.

The warning reads as follows: "A handful of sequences briefly depict a character's exposed buttocks."

The context and character butt in question remains to be seen, but fans may want to prepare for Logan's rear end to be front and center in his own video game. For some reason, this isn't quite uncharted territory for Wolverine.

Disney+ left Hugh Jackman's butt uncensored when X-Men: Days of Future Past came to the streaming service back in 2020. Deadpool & Wolverine then put the focus on Jackman's behind when it came out in 2024 and allegedly nearly doubled down on it by referring to his butt as "Canada's Ass" in one deleted scene.

It's also a shame Marvel's Wolverine will be PlayStation 5 exclusive when it launches next month, as some might remember a few lucky Xbox fans got some…unique controllers a few years back. The Xbox-exclusive "designed by Deadpool" controllers both came suited up in Deadpool & Wolverine's red and yellow superhero suit attire. They also happened to be extremely caked up.

The full ESRB description for Marvel's Wolverine can be found here: "Marvel's Wolverine is rated M for Mature 17+ by the ESRB with Blood and Gore, Drug Reference, Intense Violence, Partial Nudity, and Strong Language. Also includes In-Game Purchases. This is an action game in which players assume the role of James Logan/Wolverine, as he reunites with Team X to stop a dangerous threat. From a third-person perspective, players use melee attacks and special skills to kill enemy soldiers and robots in frenetic combat. Players use their claws to slash, stab, and slice enemies; rage modes allow players to enact faster, more destructive combos and slow-motion finishers (e.g., dramatically stabbing an enemy in the head). Combat is highlighted by frequent blood-splatter effects, screams of pain, and dismemberment/decapitation. Battlefields are sometimes strewn with torsos and limbs; cutscenes can also depict blood and gore (e.g., characters tearing enemies apart, decapitating enemy soldiers). A handful of sequences briefly depict a character's exposed buttocks. The dialogue references drugs (e.g., “It doubled my production of fentanyl.”). The words “f**k” and “sh*t” appear in the game."

We didn't really need the full ESRB description to tell us that Marvel's Wolverine will veer in a new direction for the Marvel's Spider-Man game developers at Insomniac. Pre-release footage for the game has so far promised an especially gory take on the classic comic book X-Men member, with gameplay clips showing that players will be able to rip apart any goon that gets in their way.

Marvel's Wolverine has a September 15, 2026, release date for PS5. For more, you can read IGN's interview with Insomniac from June. You can also check out everything revealed in the game's "Ain't No Hero" trailer and why some fans filled up its comment sections.

https://www.ign.com/articles/elden-ring-.title: Elden Ring Players Are Hoping for Godwyn DLC After FromSoftware Shares Cryptic Social Media Post
https://www.ign.com/articles/elden-ring-.content:
It's been two years since FromSoftware released its Shadow of the Erdtree expansion, but a new post from the developer has some fans believing that even more Elden Ring DLC is on the way.

Outside of a few updates for multiplayer spinoff Nightreign and A24's live-action movie, things have been quiet over in the Elden Ring camp. So, when the studio behind the critically acclaimed fantasy RPG franchise published a somewhat ambiguous social media post, fans wasted no time going rabid with excitement.

"Even the perilous hunt for the demigods holds moments of quiet wonder," the X/Twitter post said, accompanying a 12-second video of a player riding through Siofra River.

Even the perilous hunt for the demigods holds moments of quiet wonder.#ELDENRING pic.twitter.com/5sJyVOYi17

— ELDEN RING (@ELDENRING) July 31, 2026

It's innocuous enough on its own, but for those who have waited years for more Elden Ring DLC, it's turned into a gold mine to spin theories off of. The post itself has racked up 4.8 million views and 17.4K likes at the time of this piece's publication, with its replies filled with those who believe FromSoftware is trying to very, very subtly tell players that something is coming.

"GODWYN DLC?????" one popular quote post said.

"I am delusional please give me a second expansion," another said.

It's true that this post is a bit different from the studio's usual activity. The Elden Ring social media feed has been known to be either very direct, sharing things like announcements for updates, or extremely vague. Even then, it's hard to find a post quite like the one that has fans riled up, with few similar messages throughout 2025, if at all.

More Elden Ring dlc????! pic.twitter.com/bPjlNekm7J

— Kaida 🌊 (@khaliltooshort) July 31, 2026

FROMSOFT RELEASE GODWYN DLC AND MY LIFE IS YOURS pic.twitter.com/QSKmuNhuoh

— The Particle of God (@Vinicus1013) August 1, 2026

> HUNT for the DEMIGODS
> shows empty siofra river
> one way to get to deeproot depths is through the siofra aqueduct and transporter coffin
> GODWYN DLC ????? https://t.co/h8qZ6OU4Da

— jar saint (@scadutree) August 1, 2026

The video being set in Siofra River and the lack of giant crab and Ancestral Follower enemies also have players on edge for more Elden Ring DLC. Unfortunately, there is very little concrete evidence suggesting another expansion is on the way, at least for right now.

Besides the post itself mostly seeming to highlight one of Elden Ring's many standout moments, there are plenty of other things it could be building hype toward. The team behind the Elden Ring movie announced they had wrapped filming earlier this week ahead of its March 3, 2028, release date, for example. Our money, however, is on the Tarnished Edition that is set to come to Nintendo Switch 2 in just a few weeks.

FromSoftware is no doubt interested in pushing fans to check it and its new content out, even if it is insubstantial compared to something like Shadow of the Erdtree. Some fans have also pointed out that the video seems to feature one of Torrent's new skins, which will also be available on other platforms in the near future.

I JUST REALIZED THAT'S ONE OF THE NEW TORRENT SKINS IN THE VIDEO https://t.co/h8qZ6OU4Da pic.twitter.com/dOJ4JPp5LP

— jar saint (@scadutree) August 1, 2026

The only thing Elden Ring fans know they can look forward to in the next month is the Tarnished Edition, but that isn't stopping fans from showing up in droves to plead with FromSoftware to release another DLC expansion. There are also those showing up in the replies section to call for more content for Nightreign, while those hoping for base game DLC argue they'd rather FromSoftware return to the game that started the franchise back in 2022.

Then, of course, there are the Bloodborne fans. Poor things.

For now, FromSoftware has not confirmed a second major DLC expansion for Elden Ring. We do know that the studio has some things in development, but outside of previously announced projects like The Duskbloods, much of its future remains a mystery.

IGN called Elden Ring a "Masterpiece" in our original 10/10 review. The Shadow of the Erdtree DLC earned the same rating.

Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

https://www.ign.com/articles/dave-bautis.title: Dave Bautista in Talks to Join God of War TV Series as Kratos
https://www.ign.com/articles/dave-bautis.content:
Dave Bautista is reportedly in talks to become Kratos in Prime Video's live-action God of War TV series.

According to Variety and Deadline, Bautista has entered discussions to become PlayStation's beloved, brooding protagonist. The news comes just a few weeks after actor Ryan Hurst was dropped from the series after a bicep injury, which will require surgery. The production opted to recast Kratos as Hurst's injury means he won't be able to return to the series until sometime next year. If Bautista signs on, the plan is to get the show up and rolling again by the fall.

One advantage of Bautista provided by sources is that the actor is naturally already bulked up and wouldn't need months of training in order to get into the physique fans expect from Kratos. The actor is best known for his physical stature, having played Drax in the Guardians of the Galaxy films and hulking foes in films like Blade Runner 2049. He also has a history as a professional wrestler in the WWE, so he has the physical chops for it.

However, Bautista has lost a fair bit of weight/muscle in recent years. It's possible he's still ahead of the curve compared to most actors and could quickly put on the weight needed for Kratos, as Deadline states production won't begin until October. One other concern is that Bautista is 57 and would likely turn 58 during filming. Hurst was 50 when he got injured, meaning Bautista is just as likely, if not more, to be injured during the production of this show, especially across multiple seasons. Whether or not Amazon will put in more precautions to prevent that remains to be seen.

The actor previously campaigned to star in another adaptation of a franchise that has the GoW acronym: Gears of War. In 2018, he noted that Marcus Fenix was a "dream role" and that he'd actively been pursuing it with the rights holders. He later revealed that Universal, which was once developing Gears of War, wanted him to join the Fast and Furious franchise, but he turned it down in favor of pitching Gears of War. Now, Netflix is developing a Gears of War film, but it seems like PlayStation and Amazon may have beaten them to the punch.

Thanks to a report from MP1st, rumors also swirled over the weekend that the God of War TV series may be looking to recast Atreus actor Callum Vinson starting in season 2. It's believed this will allow the series to shoot quickly without having to wait for Vinson to grow up, as there is a three-year time jump between God of War 2018 and God of War Ragnarok, which will likely be the basis for season 2.

To top it all off, multiple new God of War games are also in the works. God of War Laufey is slated to release this coming February, while a new Kratos-led God of War game is also in development.

https://www.ign.com/articles/upcoming-so.title: Upcoming New Sony Spider-Man Universe Movies and TV Shows: 2026 Marvel Spin-Off Release Dates and Beyond
https://www.ign.com/articles/upcoming-so.content:
Spider-Man is one of the few Marvel heroes with a supporting cast and rogues gallery wide enough to support an entire cinematic universe. Or so execs at Sony thought when they launched their Spider-Man Universe of spin-off movies and TV shows. But now there are only a handful of projects left on that slate, the most notable of course being Tom Holland's live-action Spidey movies, a likely new trilogy of which kicked off with Spider-Man: Brand New Day. Meanwhile, Madame Web, Morbius, and Kraven came, went, and will never be forgotten, the Venom trilogy has run its course, Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse is getting another sequel after Across the Spider-Verse, and the Spider-Man Noir series debuted in May of 2026 with Nic Cage playing the title character.

While the latest word is that Sony is now looking to reboot its Spider-Man shared universe, there are still some projects moving forward (and several that are in limbo).

To help make sense of the various Spider-Man-adjacent projects in development, we're breaking down every Sony Marvel movie or show that's either been officially announced or rumored to be in the works. Check out the slideshow gallery below or scroll down to get the scoop on Spidey's cinematic future.

What Are the Next Spider-Man Spin-Off Movies and TV Shows Coming Out? 2026 Release Dates

Here's a quick bullet list of all the movies and TV shows that are in various stages of development:

  • Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse (In Production) - June 18, 2027
  • Spider-Man: Brand New Day Sequel (In Development)
  • Venom Animated Movie (In Development)
  • Sony's Spider-Man Universe Reboot Movie (Status Unknown)
  • Spider-Noir Season 2 (Status Unknown)
  • Silk: Spider Society Series (Presumed Cancelled)
  • Untitled Female Cast Into the Spider-Verse Spin-Off (Presumed Cancelled)

Read on for more details on each project.

Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse (June 18, 2027)

Status: In Production

The third Spider-Verse film is called Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse (dropping the Part One and Part Two from the Into the Spider-Verse sequels' titles that had previously been announced). Obviously Across the Spider-Verse, the second film in the series, leaves a lot of questions that will need to be answered in Beyond. Beyond the Spider-Verse was expected to be released on March 29, 2024, but in July of 2023, Sony changed several of its slate's release dates, including this film. It is now expected to be released on June 18, 2027. Learn more about the Spider-Verse here.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day Sequel

Status: In Development

It was unclear after Spider-Man: No Way Home's release in 2021 when the next appearance of Tom Holland's wallcrawler would come. When Sony and Marvel made a new deal in 2019 to continue to share the character, which allowed No Way Home to be made, an MCU crossover film was also said to be part of that agreement. What that crossover film might be and what its status is remains unclear, although it seems almost certain that Holland will appear in Avengers: Secret Wars at the very least (and certainly the Brand New Day post-credits scene supports the idea of some kind of spidery appearance in that film or Avengers: Doomsday).

Regardless, now that Spider-Man: Brand New Day is a huge hit, you can be sure Holland and friends will return alongside director Destin Daniel Cretton for whatever Spider-Man 5: Holland Edition winds up being called. It's generally assumed that Brand New Day is the start of a new trilogy, something producer Amy Pascal hinted at all the way back when No Way Home was coming out.

Venom Animated Movie

Status: In Development

While it doesn't appear we're getting any further live-action Venom sequels starring Tom Hardy, the Lethal Protector is making the jump to the animated realm. THR reports that Final Destination: Bloodlines duo Zach Lipovsky and Adam B. Stein are set to direct a feature-length animated Venom movie. If it's even half as good as the Spider-Verse films, Venom fans will have reason to celebrate.

Sony's Spider-Man Universe Reboot Movie

Status: Unknown

Things have been pretty quiet on the Sony's Spider-Man Universe front since the release of Kraven the Hunter in 2024. Now we know that Sony is basically canning this shared universe and maybe starting from scratch again eventually. Sony Pictures CEO Tom Rothman said in February, 2026, that a reboot is in the works following Kraven's abysmal box office performance. So don't expect a follow-up to the Knull tease from 2024's Venom: The Last Dance.

However, when Spider-Man: Brand New Day was released, he said the following regarding plans to expand the Spidey universe: "Right now, we don’t know. ... We never looked at it as the 'Sony-Marvel Universe.' We looked at if there were worthwhile movies to make with other characters. At the moment, there are none in active development." Sure you did, Tom.

Still, with any luck the next shared universe will actually feature Spider-Man this time.

Spider-Noir Season 2

Status: Unknown

Following the announcement of Silk: Spider Society (see below), word came that Spider-Man Noir was the second series to come about from Sony and Prime Video's partnership. And indeed, the Spider-Man Noir series -- officially titled Spider-Noir -- wound up taking shape before Spider Society. A live-action show set in a Depression-era version of the Marvel Universe, it features Nic Cage as Ben Reilly -- not Peter Parker. Also known as The Spider, he's a gumshoe detective who also has spider powers.

The show comes from Into the Spider-Verse producers Phil Lord and Christopher Miller and 22 Jump Street writer Orien Uziel, who serves as co-showrunner with Steve Lightfoot (Netflix's The Punisher).

Whether or not a Season 2 will happen remains to be seen, but we sure hope it does. As IGN's Jim Vejvoda said in his review of Season 1, "Cage’s Bogie-meets-Bugs Bunny pulp hero invigorates the highly entertaining, genre-bending Spider-Noir."

Whether or not a Season 2 of Spider-Noir will happen remains to be seen, but we sure hope it does.

Silk: Spider Society Series

Status: Presumed Cancelled

A more recent addition to Spider-Man's world, Silk is a heroine who was bitten by the same radioactive spider that gave Peter Parker his powers. Resurfacing after a decade spent locked in an underground bunker, Cindy Moon has followed the example of Spider-Man and become a costumed superhero. Cindy has actually made small appearances in Spider-Man: Homecoming and Avengers: Infinity War (played by Tiffany Espensen). But we assume the role would be recast for any new Silk project.

Silk was originally announced as a movie, but eventually evolved into a series that was meant to air on MGM+ and Prime Video (the first in a new partnership between Sony, MGM and Prime Video). Into the Spider-Verse's Angela Kang was to serve as showrunner, and the series would follow Cindy's origin story as she escapes imprisonment, comes to terms with her powers and seeks out her missing family. However, in May of 2024, Variety reported that the show was dropped by Amazon/MGM+ and that Sony would be trying to shop it to other buyers. There has been no word on the show since then.

Untitled Female Cast Into the Spider-Verse Spin-Off

Status: Presumed Cancelled

An Into the Spider-Verse spin-off featuring an all-female cast was said to be in the works at one point, with Spider-Gwen expected to make her return. Other characters like Spider-Girl, Spider-Woman, Madame Web, Silk and even Black Cat might've been featured. Not much has been heard of this project since it was first revealed in 2018, however, and it seems likely to have died on the vine (web?).

Unrealized Spider-Man Spin-Off Projects

There has been a host of rumored or reported Spider-Man spinoff movies over the years that have never actually gotten made. Along with Venom, one of the earliest Spider-Man spinoff movies Sony pursued was Silver & Black, a team-up film featuring mercenary Silver Sable and master thief/occasional Spider-Man love interest Black Cat. While Sony went as far as hiring director Gina Prince-Bythewood (The Secret Life of Bees) and dating the film for a February 2019 release, it was eventually canceled. Last we heard, the studio was reworking Silver & Black into solo movies for the characters, though presumably those projects have stalled out at this point. In 2020, reports indicated that Black Cat and Silver Sable might become TV projects for Sony instead.

Variety reported in March 2018 that director Spike Lee was in talks to direct a Nightwatch film, though Lee has since said he is not attached. The vigilante hero wears a durable nanotechnology costume that enhances his strength by stimulating his adrenal glands, but apparently is not capable of getting him out of development hell.

Another fairly recent addition to the Spider-Man universe, Jackpot has often fought alongside Spider-Man in defense of New York City. When she was first introduced, readers were led to believe she was actually Mary Jane Watson in disguise. Instead, it was eventually revealed that Jackpot is an identity used by two different women - genetic researcher Sara Ehret and her admirer, Alana Jobson. It was reported in August 2018 that a Jackpot movie was in development, and in 2020 further news came that Marc Guggenheim was writing the screenplay. No cast or director have been revealed so far and this one also seems unlikely to happen at this point.

At CinemaCon 2022, Sony announced El Muerto, a Spider-Man spin-off movie starring musician, producer, actor, and wrestler Bad Bunny as the title character. El Muerto is a wrestler with superpowers whose mask and abilities are passed down from generation to generation. The film was reported to have a release date of January 12, 2024, at that time, and yet as of April, 2023, filming had still not begun and Bad Bunny's publicist said the film was "at a standstill," only to later clarify that it was "in development." On June 21, 2023, a Sony press release said that the film had moved to a TBD date. And in September, 2023, Bad Bunny seemed to tell Vanity Fair that he had dropped out of the film. Hmmm...

Sony Pictures Entertainment execs clearly have plans for the Marvel characters they have the rights to. “We have the next seven or eight years laid out as to what we’re going to do with that asset, and that will not only be on the film side -- it’ll be on the TV side,” said Sony Pictures Entertainment chairman Tony Vinciquerra. “Our television group will have its own set of characters from within that universe that we will seek to develop.” Of course, that was in 2019, so we're already seven years into his seven!

Could the Olivia Wilde-directed Spider-Woman movie that was reported on in 2020 still be in the works? Or the Roberto Orci-scripted Marvel project that was also rumored that year? How many of the projects already reported on fall under Vinciquerra's plans, or have been dropped by now? Madame Web probably already knows, but for the rest of us, time will tell.

For even more on this series, be sure to check out how to watch Sony's Spider-Man Universe Movies in chronological order.

Returning for its third year, Ludwig’s Streamer Games hosted by creator Ludwig Ahgren again brought together some of the top online content creators to compete in live physical challenges, ranging from intense sporting events to schoolyard games with an amped up twist. Alienware was an official partner at the event, offering attendees free swag and the chance to win some cool prizes.

A total of 40 familiar and popular faces participated in the competition, which took place August 1–2. Reflecting the growing popularity of the event, this year’s Streamer Games was at its biggest venue yet, USC’s Allyson Felix Field in Los Angeles. And as Ludwig noted, this time they included many more competitors representing more countries from around the world.

The eight teams facing off were:
